## Summary

Snapback 4 is one of two parallel candidates for the successor to Snapback 2,
and the sibling of Snapback 3, not its successor. It builds
[LLP 2000.000](./2000.000-keep-the-core-flip-two-substrates.rfc.md) as
written: the Snapback 2 core kept verbatim, two substrates flipped up front —
resources metered at runtime instead of priced statically, and a client that
replicates the viewer's declared partition instead of caching receipted
results — proved first on the hub fixture, with a deterministic simulator as
the primary harness. Snapback 3 ([LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md), led by
Codex / GPT-6 Astra) keeps the same two questions open and discovers their
answers in its first slice. Snapback 2 ([LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md))
continues as the incumbent and the control. All three are judged by one
pre-registered comparison on one clock.

This document records the author's decisions of 2026-09-12 that created the
track, restates the bet on one page so a reader can orient without the brief,
fixes the bakeoff protocol, draws the fence, and plans the first four weeks.
The design argument and its evidence stay in LLP 2000.000. Only running code
will bind (`rules/RULES.md`).

## 1. Decisions (author, 2026-09-12)

On 2026-09-12 Charlie Cheever asked whether Claude Fable 5.1 should lead a
Snapback 4 while Codex / GPT-6 Astra leads Snapback 3 and Snapback 2
continues, "and see which one turns out best." The lead answered yes with
conditions; the author accepted them ("Sounds good") and asked for this
document. The decisions below are therefore the lead's proposal as accepted
by the author. Where the author has not separately ruled, the text says so.

1. **Three tracks, one comparison.** Snapback 2 continues as the incumbent
   and the control. Snapback 3 builds LLP 2000; Snapback 4 builds LLP
   2000.000. This is a bakeoff of *bets* — discover the substrates in the
   slice versus decide them first — not of models. The result will say more
   about the bets than about the leads, and §3 is written so that it can.
2. **The name is Snapback 4.** Siblings, not a sequence: "4" does not mean
   "after 3." A separate number gives the track its own corpus root,
   directory, package identity and data directory with no rename when the
   bakeoff resolves, and files never move in LLP. If Snapback 4 loses, it is
   a number that never shipped. "Snapback 3b" was considered and rejected:
   it reads as a variant of 3, and this is a different bet.
3. **Snapback 4 builds LLP 2000.000 as written.** Its §14 open questions are
   the lead's to decide inside the track, recorded in §7 as they are
   decided. The author rules on the bar, the comparison and promotion (§3).
4. **One owner on the core.** The lead writes the engine, the store and the
   client contract. Codex lanes build the fixture generator, the reference
   applications, the device witnesses and the periphery. Blind reviews from
   two model families are reserved for the two disclosure-sensitive
   mechanisms: partition inversion of read rules (LLP 2000.000 §7.1) and
   the meter's cut behaviour on non-uniform scans (LLP 2000.000 §6). This
   departs from the standing rule that Codex codes and Claude orchestrates,
   deliberately, for the core only.
5. **The clock is four weeks** from the first commit under `snapback4/` to
   the first slice running on the hub fixture. At the clock the author kills
   the track, merges its substrates into a survivor, or continues it. There
   is no third month without a ruling.
6. **Shared and not shared.** Shared with Snapback 3: the LLP corpus, the
   Clique harness and scorers, the fixtures, the briefs, and the simulator
   once either track has one. Not shared: code, except the Snapback 2 pieces
   both are expected to copy (LLP 2000.000 §5.1).
7. **Snapback 2 keeps shipping and freezes new substrate work for the
   duration.** Fix-forward, the loop bar, acquisition and papercuts continue;
   no new certificate axes, client custody mechanisms or ceiling changes.
   This is accepted here as a condition of the bakeoff. Making it binding on
   concurrent Snapback 2 sessions needs one line in `rules/NOT-DOING.md`'s
   Moves ledger, which this document does not write.
8. **Reading load.** This root, updated in place, and one append-only
   journal, `snapback4/JOURNAL.md`. Sub-LLPs only for a decision that must
   outlive the journal. No panels beyond decision 4's two reviews.

## 2. The bet on one page

**Keep verbatim from Snapback 2** (LLP 2000.000 §5.1): the rule language
with its uniformity and hoist analysis, `decided_true` and the
structural-fact refusals; one data language, Quarry, with `--` comments,
`require … else CODE`, `shape`, `merge`, `walk`, `chunk`; the value model
and its conformance corpus; typed read and write states with no silent state
and the refusal envelope `{code, family, site, message, rewrite, guide}`; the
successor classifier (widening additive, checked narrowing, exact projection
ownership); `deliver`'s engine-computed audience, tombstones and
`bootstrap`; `schedule`, `job`, `chunk` and rehearsal; personas; `init`,
`dev`, `check`, `doctor`, `run`, `test`, `why`, `trace`, `guide`; H0
`deploy`, `rollback`, `secret`; channels; assets; the word-prefix index.

**Flip 1 — certify authorization, meter resources** (LLP 2000.000 §6). The
certificate keeps every read site's shape, uniformity, completeness class
and prediction eligibility, and stops pricing bytes and steps. A
deterministic meter charges examined rows, index entries, rule probes,
steps, heap, output and rows written as the program runs, on the server and
in the client interpreter alike. A query cut by the meter returns `capped`
with no continuation past the cut, the same observable outcome as a static
ceiling cut today; a mutation aborts with `E_BOUND` naming actual work; a
job is chunked. `check --cost` prints the structural cost class; `test`
prints measured meters on the hub fixture.
# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.

 Spellings are illustrative. None of the blocks below is a compiling example.
 
+### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
+
+Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
+64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
+`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
+The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
+identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
+adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
+address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
+
+The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
+aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
+marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
+of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
+target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
+generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
+together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
+are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
+it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
+zero.
+
 ### 3.1 F1: maintained columns
 
 F1 is LLP 3000.007.001, unchanged. Its value here is ranking. With `likeCount`

+expired. When the expiry is due, retirement removes the root and pending-opening
+entry and applies its declared `on delete cascade`, `set null` and `restrict`
+actions in one transaction (LLP 3000.039 §3). A live restrict child or physical
+read-through child may retain the root physically, but the expired root remains
+absent from all logical reads. Cleanup advances past such retained roots and
+preserves its bounded scan position across calls; cascade/set-null writes and
+the root removal either commit together or roll back together. The same action
+path governs a row born expired at commit and an expired predecessor retired
+for a same-id insertion, so neither inline cleanup path can create an orphan.
+
+Expiring a never-opened root creates no root deletion event, because no device
+could hold it. Its actions can still change opened children, and those ordinary
+row changes carry their partition events. Deleting an opened row keeps the
 ordinary revocation and retention semantics.

+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_META: &str = "maintained_id_version";
+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION: &str = "sha256-v1";
+
+/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.
+/// Programs address aggregates by their group index, never by this internal
+/// id. Domain separation makes future encodings explicit migrations.
+// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — every aggregate writer, synthetic check row and adoption rebuild shares this bounded identity.
 pub fn maintained_id(key: &[Value]) -> String {
-    crate::value::canonical_json(&key)
+    crate::value::digest(&("snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1", key))
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);
+    let long = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".repeat(100_000))]);
+    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(short, long);
+    assert_ne!(short, crate::value::digest(&[Value::String("x".into())]));
 }

+#[test]
+fn missing_identity_marker_rebuilds_a_principal_reference_and_max_text_group() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  owner: principal\n  parent: parents\n  token: text <=64\n  amount: int\n  public\nview totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    let owner = format!("user:{}", "o".repeat(59));
+    let parent = "p".repeat(64);
+    let token = "t".repeat(64);
+    assert_eq!((owner.len(), parent.len(), token.len()), (64, 64, 64));
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("owner", Value::Id(owner.clone())),
+            ("parent", Value::Id(parent.clone())), ("token", Value::String(token.clone())), ("amount", Value::Int(7))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(owner), Value::Id(parent), Value::String(token)]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    let after = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
+    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
+    // on every newly published schema/projection.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();
+    assert!(encoded.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}

+#[test]
+fn authoritative_memory_sweeps_resume_and_wrap_past_restricted_roots() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut store = snapback4_device::memory::MemoryStore::new();
+    store.activate_server_at(bound.schema, 0).unwrap();
+    store.seed_server_at([
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}

+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let required =
+        snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&bound.schema.public_projection());
+    assert!(
+        required
+            .capabilities
+            .contains(&"maintained-id-sha256-v1".to_owned())
+    );
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities
+        .retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(
+        refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"),
+        "{refusal:?}"
+    );
+}

   101	    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade

   106	        parent: &str,
   107	        id: &Value,
   108	        deleting: &BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
   109	    ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

   111	            .schema
   112	            .children(parent)
   113	            .map(|(n, _, _)| {

   115	                // index scan. Identities from other closure tables cannot
   116	                // consume a row in this table's prefix.

   128	            for (name, limit) in &children {

   133	            Ok(occupied)

   102	                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
   103	                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
   104	            }
   105	            return Ok(None);
   106	        }
   107	        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())

   110	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   111	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
   112	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
   113	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
   114	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
   115	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
   116	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
   117	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
   118	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
   119	        }
   120	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
   121	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
   122	        for maintain in maintains {
   123	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
   124	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
   125	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
   126	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
   127	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
   128	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
   129	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
   130	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
   131	            result?;
   132	        }
   133	        Ok(())
   134	    }

   136	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   137	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   138	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   139	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   140	        let result = work(self);
   141	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   142	        result
   143	    }

   145	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   146	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   147	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   148	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   149	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   150	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   151	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   152	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   153	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   154	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   155	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   156	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   157	        }
   158	        for (key, change) in changes {
   159	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   160	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   161	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   162	                continue;
   163	            }
   164	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   165	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   166	            }
   167	        }
   168	        Ok(())
   169	    }

   171	    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
   172	    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
   173	    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   174	        let schema = self.schema;
   175	        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
   176	            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
   177	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   178	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   179	            }
   180	        }
   181	        Ok(())
   182	    }

   185	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain_reported(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, report: &mut crate::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   186	        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
   187	        self.rebuilt_source_rows = 0;
   188	        self.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
   189	        let rows = self.rebuilt_source_rows;
   190	        report.views.push(crate::store::adoption_report::ViewBuild { name: maintain.label(), rows, elapsed: started.elapsed() });

   194	    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
   195	    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
   196	    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
   197	    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
   198	    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
   199	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   200	    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain], previous: Option<&crate::schema::Schema>, activation_tx: Option<&crate::store::Tx<'_>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   201	        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
   202	        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
   203	            // The durable legacy address is the predecessor's canonical
   204	            // logical group tuple. Decode that address with predecessor types:
   205	            // candidate projection may already have removed predecessor group
   206	            // columns when adoption also changes the maintain declaration.
   207	            let identity_schema = previous.unwrap_or(self.schema);
   208	            let identity_maintain = identity_schema.maintain_for(&maintain.target)
   209	                .filter(|old| old.private.is_none() && old.row_key.is_none())
   210	                .unwrap_or(maintain);
   211	            let identity_target = identity_schema.table(&maintain.target)
   212	                .unwrap_or_else(|| &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]);
   213	            let fields: Vec<_> = identity_maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
   214	                let kind = identity_target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
   215	                (field, kind)
   216	            }).collect();
   217	            let mut rows = Vec::new();
   218	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   219	            loop {
   220	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   221	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   222	                for (row, encoded) in page {
   223	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   224	                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   225	                    let address = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
   226	                        .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
   227	                    let values = match address {
   228	                        Some(key) => key,
   229	                        None => fields.iter().map(|(field, _)| Ok(row.field(field)?.clone()))
   230	                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?,
   231	                    };
   232	                    let key: Vec<_> = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
   233	                    rows.push((old, key));
   234	                }
   235	            }
   236	            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
   237	        }
   238	
   239	        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   240	        let mut settled = false;
   241	        // One dependency edge can settle per pass.  Count identities rather
   242	        // than target tables: one aggregate target may contain an arbitrary
   243	        // acyclic chain of references to other rows in that same target.
   244	        let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
   245	        // The first pass also materializes empty target maps, so retain one
   246	        // additional observation pass even when every target is empty.
   247	        for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
   248	            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   249	            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
   250	                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
   251	                for (old, key) in rows {
   252	                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
   253	                        let mut value = value.clone();
   254	                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
   255	                        value
   256	                    }).collect();
   257	                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
   258	                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
   259	                }
   260	            }
   261	            if next_ids == ids {
   262	                ids = next_ids;
   263	                settled = true;
   264	                break;
   265	            }
   266	            ids = next_ids;
   267	        }
   268	        if !settled {
   269	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
   270	        }
   271	
   272	        // Release retention is part of the store: a hidden row or column may
   273	        // still name an aggregate target that remains active through adoption.
   274	        // Rewrite its image and reference ledger in this transaction too.
   275	        let mut rewritten = match activation_tx {
   276	            Some(tx) => crate::store::dormant::rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(tx, &ids)?,
   277	            None => 0,
   278	        };
   279	
   280	        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   281	            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
   282	                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
   283	                .collect();
   284	            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
   285	        }).collect();
   286	        for (name, table, columns) in references {
   287	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   288	            loop {
   289	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   290	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   291	                for (old, encoded) in page {
   292	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   293	                    let mut next = old.clone();
   294	                    let mut changed = false;
   295	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   296	                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
   297	                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
   298	                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
   299	                        }
   300	                    }
   301	                    if changed {
   302	                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
   303	                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   304	                    }
   305	                }
   306	            }
   307	        }
   308	        Ok(rewritten)
   309	    }

   311	    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
   312	    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
   313	    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
   314	    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
   315	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   316	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   317	        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
   318	        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
   319	        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
   320	        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
   321	        self.column_rebuild = saved;
   322	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   323	        result
   324	    }

   387	    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
   388	        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())

   391	    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
   392	    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
   393	    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
   394	    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   395	        // One returned source image and its encoded key (MemoryRows also materializes count_prefix).
   396	        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);

   398	            let source = &runner.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   399	            let index = maintain.contribution_index();
   400	            if !source.indexes.contains_key(&index) { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("maintain {} needs its contribution index", maintain.target))); }
   401	            runner.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   402	            let present = runner.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, &maintain.source, &index, key, 1))? != 0;
   403	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — a local positive witness keeps zero; absence needs complete, currently held source coverage.
   404	            if !present && runner.device && !runner.aggregate_source_complete(maintain, key)? {
   405	                runner.unknown_fact(&maintain.source, &index, key, "zero-sum occupancy");
   406	                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the zero-sum group's source occupancy is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   407	            }
   408	            Ok(present)
   409	        })
   410	    }

   412	    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   413	        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   414	        if source.sync.as_ref().is_none_or(|sync| sync.horizon.is_some()) || self.schema.maintain_subset_unknown(&maintain.target) { return Ok(false); }

   416	        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_group_key(maintain, key))? { return Ok(false); }

   418	            let values = index.columns().iter().map_while(|column| maintain.by.iter().position(|field| field == column).map(|n| key[n].clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   419	            if self.retained_group(&maintain.source, name, &values)? { return Ok(false); }
   420	        }
   421	        Ok(true)
   422	    }

   424	    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   425	        if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(&maintain.target)) {
   426	            return Err(super::timeline::refusal("E_TIMELINE_OWNED", "timeline-owned tables cannot be aggregate targets; maintain a mapped application table instead"));
   427	        }
   428	        let id = maintained_id(&key);
   429	        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
   430	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   431	        let existing = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &maintain.target, &id))?;
   432	        let target_key = target_group_key(maintain, &key);
   433	        if self.device && existing.is_none() && !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key)? {
   434	            self.unknown_fact(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key, "aggregate base");
   435	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the affected aggregate value or its absence is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   436	        }
   437	        let old_value = existing.as_ref().and_then(|row| row.field("value").ok()).map(Value::as_int).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);
   438	        let next = i128::from(old_value) + change;
   439	        if !(I53_MIN as i128..=I53_MAX as i128).contains(&next) {
   440	            return Err(aggregate_overflow(maintain));
   441	        }
   442	        let keep_zero = next == 0 && self.live_sum(maintain) && match source_present {
   443	            Some(present) => present,
   444	            None => self.aggregate_source_present(maintain, &key)?,
   445	        };
   446	        if next == 0 && !keep_zero {
   447	            if let Some(existing) = existing {
   448	                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
   449	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   450	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   451	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   452	            }
   453	            self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, 0)?;
   454	            return Ok(());
   455	        }
   456	        let mut row = crate::small_map::collect([("id".to_owned(), Value::Id(id.clone())), ("value".to_owned(), Value::Int(next as i64))]);
   457	        for (field, value) in maintain.group_fields().iter().zip(key.iter().cloned()) {
   458	            row.insert(field.clone(), value);
   459	        }
   460	        // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#3-global-maintained-view-representation — stores index the one logical empty group by a hidden constant.
   461	        if maintain.by.is_empty() { row.insert(GLOBAL.into(), Value::Bool(true)); }

   463	        if existing.as_ref() == Some(&row) { return Ok(()); }
   464	        let entries = self.tx.put(&maintain.target, target, &row, existing.as_ref())?;
   465	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   466	        self.row_changed(&maintain.target, existing.as_ref(), Some(&row), Origin::Maintained)?;
   467	        self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, next as i64)
   468	    }
   469	}

   471	pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {
   472	    Ok(match &maintain.kind {
   473	        MaintainKind::Count => i128::from(direction),
   474	        MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(direction).checked_mul(i128::from(source.field(of)?.as_int()?)).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?,
   475	    })
   476	}

   479	pub(super) fn aggregate_overflow(maintain: &Maintain) -> RuntimeError {
   480	    RuntimeError::AggregateOverflow { maintain: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| maintain.target.clone(), |o|o.table.clone()), column: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| "value".into(), |o|o.column.clone()) }

     1	//! The interpreter on a device (LLP 2000.000 §7.2, §9): the same programs
     2	//! the server runs, over the rows the device holds — its partition — where
     3	//! delivered rows are readable as held; provisional images need current read
     4	//! authority. Unknown authorization, unknown online-only facts and reads
     5	//! past a horizon make the result `complete: false`. A mutation
     6	//! predicts: its rows are written to the device's store for the host to
     7	//! mark pending, and the server judges the write when it arrives.
     8	
     9	use super::runner::Runner;
    10	use super::validate::validate_device_inputs as validate_inputs;
    11	use super::{Context, QueryOutcome};
    12	use crate::error::{Refusal, RuntimeError};
    13	use crate::ir::Program;
    14	use crate::meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter};
    15	use crate::rows::Rows;
    16	use crate::schema::Schema;
    17	use crate::value::Value;

    19	// @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — a query entry must not execute a server-only mutation under Cut::Cap.
    20	pub fn require_query(program: &Program) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    21	    if program.kind != crate::ir::ProgramKind::Query {
    22	        return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{} is not a query; use its mutation, job or action entry", program.name)));
    23	    }
    24	    Ok(())
    25	}

    27	/// A query over the device's rows.
    28	pub fn query(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
    29	    query_with_coverage(rows, schema, program, context, ceilings).0
    30	}
    31	
    32	/// Unknown means the server can establish a missing fact or presence; preserve it, and whether incompleteness is exclusively retained history, even after a require/unwrap refusal.
    33	pub fn query_with_coverage(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool) {
    34	    let (result, unknown, retained, _, _) = observe_query(rows, schema, program, context, ceilings, false);
    35	    (result, unknown, retained)
    36	}

    38	pub fn query_with_components(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool, std::collections::BTreeMap<String, super::components::Coverage>) {
    39	    let (result, unknown, retained, components, _) = observe_query(rows, schema, program, context, ceilings, true);
    40	    (result, unknown, retained, components)
    41	}
    42	
    43	pub fn observe_query(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, mut context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings, components: bool) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool, std::collections::BTreeMap<String, super::components::Coverage>, super::components::Provenance) {
    44	    if let Err(error) = require_query(program) { return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default(), Default::default()); }
    45	    if let Err(error) = validate_inputs(schema, program, &mut context.args) { return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default(), Default::default()); }
    46	    context.row_provenance |= schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.leave == crate::schema::LeavePolicy::DeliveredHistory);
    47	    let meter = if let Some(spent) = context.read_spent {
    48	        match Meter::resume(ceilings, spent) {
    49	            Ok(meter) => meter,
    50	            Err(error) => return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default(), Default::default()),
    51	        }
    52	    } else { Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Cap) };
    53	    let mut runner = Runner::new(rows, schema, context, meter, 0);
    54	    runner.device = true;
    55	    runner.component_observation = components;
    56	    let result = (|| {
    57	    let data = match runner.run(program) {
    58	        Ok(data) => data,
    59	        // A require/unwrap after an unheld card is no more authoritative
    60	        // than a null card; the original query must be answered remotely.
    61	        Err(_) if runner.query_unavailable => Value::Null,
    62	        Err(error) => return Err(error.refusal()),
    63	    };
    64	    // @ref LLP 3000.016#2.2 — withheld work keeps its execution charges, but discarded data is not published output.
    65	    let data = if runner.query_unavailable { Value::Null } else { data };
    66	    let capped = runner.meter.capped_at.is_some();
    67	    let charged = runner.charge_output(&data);
    68	    if !capped && runner.meter.capped_at.is_some() { runner.components.note(|frame| frame.capped = true); }
    69	    charged?;
    70	    let next = if runner.query_unavailable { None } else { runner.outcome_next_cursor()? };    Ok(QueryOutcome { decoration_expiry: runner.decoration_expiry, search_rows: runner.search_rows.take(), search_scopes: None,
    71	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] delivery: None,
    72	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] delivery_meter: None, ephemeral: None,
    73	        unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,
    74	        complete: runner.meter.capped_at.is_none() && runner.word_cut_at.is_none() && !runner.non_uniform && !runner.page_overflow && !runner.value_source_incomplete && !runner.page_position_lost() && !runner.timeline_pending && !runner.beyond_horizon && !runner.presence_unknown,
    75	        cut: runner.read_cut(),
    76	        capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
    77	        word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),
    78	        next,
    79	        data,
    80	        seq: 0,
    81	        metered: runner.meter.used,
    82	        tables: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect(),
    83	        next_expiry: runner.next_expiry.get(),
    84	        // A device never knows presence, so it names nothing to follow.
    85	    })
    86	    })();
    87	    let components = if result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|outcome| matches!(outcome.data, Value::Row(_))) { runner.component_coverage() } else { Default::default() };
    88	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.22.1 — presence is server knowledge too; a resource or structural cut is not.
    89	    (result, runner.missing_fact.is_some() || runner.presence_unknown, runner.only_retained_incomplete() && (!schema.operations.get(&program.name).is_some_and(|f| f.search_decoration) || runner.retained_seen), components, runner.components.provenance())}

    91	/// What a mutation predicts on the device: its result, and the tables it
    92	/// wrote through the store. A refusal is the caller's to show; the host
    93	/// rolls its transaction back.
    94	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
    95	pub struct Prediction {
    96	    pub new_ids: Vec<String>,
    97	    pub result: Value,
    98	    pub written: Vec<String>,
    99	    pub read: Vec<String>,
   100	}
   101	
   102	pub fn predict(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, mut context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> Result<Prediction, RuntimeError> {
   103	    if program.kind == crate::ir::ProgramKind::Action { return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp("an action cannot predict; call client.act".into())); }
   104	    validate_inputs(schema, program, &mut context.args)?;
   105	    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — compiler facts are required for receipt prediction.
   106	    // Missing classification (legacy/raw IR callers) conservatively keeps custody.
   107	    if !schema.receipts.is_empty() && !schema.operations.get(&program.name).is_some_and(|fact| matches!(fact.predicts.as_deref(), Some("eligible" | "never"))) {
   108	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt mutation has no compiler classification".into()));
   109	    }
   110	    if let Some(reason) = schema.prediction_reservation_refusal(program) {
   111	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(reason.into()));
   112	    }
   113	    // Runtime custody is independent of advisory prediction classification.
   114	    if schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| program.name == f.delivered || program.name == f.seen || program.name == f.compact) {
   115	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt reports need server settlement".into()));
   116	    }
   117	    if let Some(fact) = schema.operations.get(&program.name) && fact.predicts.as_deref() == Some("never") {
   118	        let reason = fact.sites.iter().find(|site| site.class == crate::schema::SiteClass::Server).map(|site| format!("site {}: {}", site.site, site.reason)).unwrap_or_else(|| program.name.clone());
   119	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("{reason}; queued without a predicted row")));
   120	    }
   121	    // Classification metadata is advisory. Even an edge no-op queues as a
   122	    // whole mutation; no actual transition hook would run for that case.
   123	    if !schema.timelines.is_empty() && crate::ir::write_tables(program).iter().any(|(table, _)| schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| &t.edges[0] == table)) {
   124	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("timeline follow/unfollow/refollow requires online-only slot accounting".into()));
   125	    }
   126	    let mut runner = Runner::new(rows, schema, context, Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Abort), 0);
   127	    runner.device = true;
   128	    runner.device_allowance = Some(Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Abort));
   129	    let result = runner.run(program).and_then(|value| {
   130	        // The server retires every born/updated-expired final image before
   131	        // final obligations. Prediction must publish that same action closure
   132	        // or queue/refuse when device coverage cannot prove it.
   133	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — commit-end expiry actions are part of the predicted transaction.
   134	        runner.device_work(|runner| runner.retire_expired_births())?;
   135	        runner.check_final_exists()?;
   136	        if runner.receipt_allocation { runner.charge_output(&value)?; }
   137	        Ok(value)
   138	    });
   139	    if matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { .. })) {
   140	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("authorization work allowance exhausted; queued without a prediction".into()));
   141	    }
   142	    // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — a provisional ordinal is not server evidence.
   143	    // Any refusal after consuming one may change with the server's assignment,
   144	    // including constraints, postconditions and a selected branch's refusal.
   145	    // The host rolls back all predicted rows and retains the intent.
   146	    // Receipt dependencies are classified before evaluation (LLP 3000.022 §14.3).
   147	    if runner.receipt_allocation && result.is_err() {
   148	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt allocation preceded a refusal; queue the write for server settlement (guide writes)".into()));
   149	    }
   150	    if runner.reservation_deferred && matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::Bound { .. })) {
   151	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("deferred maintenance reservation exhausted; queue for server settlement".into()));
   152	    }
   153	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — a refusal after an insert this device could not prove may not be
   154	    // the server's (it can refuse that insert first): the write queues and the server's verdict stands.
   155	    if runner.unproved_write && result.as_ref().is_err_and(|error| error.is_refusal() && !matches!(error, RuntimeError::Prediction(_))) {
   156	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("refusal after an unproved insert".into()));
   157	    }
   158	    if runner.provisional_sequence_read && result.is_err() {
   159	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("a refusal depends on a provisional sequence; queue the write for the server (guide writes)".into()));
   160	    }
   161	    // Unknown input can select a branch the server will never execute. Its
   162	    // exhaustion cannot refuse the write; a cut with known inputs still can.
   163	    if matches!(&result, Err(RuntimeError::Bound { .. })) && !runner.charged_untaken && runner.missing_fact.is_none() {
   164	        return Err(result.unwrap_err());
   165	    }
   166	    if runner.beyond_horizon {
   167	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(runner.missing_fact.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{}: this device cannot establish a read needed to predict", program.name))));
   168	    }
   169	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#19.1 — a meter cut after paying an untaken presence arm is the prediction's, not the write's: the server may skip that arm and succeed, so the write queues without a row.
   170	    let counterfactual = |error: RuntimeError, charged: bool| match error {
   171	        RuntimeError::Bound { .. } if charged => RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("{error}; the prediction paid an untaken presence arm the server may skip; queued without a predicted row")),
   172	        other => other,
   173	    };
   174	    let result = result.map_err(|error| counterfactual(error, runner.charged_untaken))?;
   175	    if !runner.receipt_allocation {
   176	        let charged = runner.charged_untaken;
   177	        runner.charge_output(&result).map_err(|error| {
   178	            if runner.unproved_write && error.is_refusal() {
   179	                RuntimeError::Prediction("refusal after an unproved insert".into())
   180	            } else { counterfactual(error, charged) }
   181	        })?;
   182	    }
   183	    Ok(Prediction { new_ids: runner.context.minted_ids.clone(), result, written: runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect(), read: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect() })
   184	}

   186	/// A native read over the device's rows (LLP 3000.005 §9): the app's module,
   187	/// the same one the server runs, over what the device holds, with the
   188	/// device's words — a page at the horizon or an online-only table is
   189	/// `complete: false`; unknown coverage is what the host falls back on.
   190	#[cfg(feature = "wasm-host")]
   191	pub fn native_query(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, module: &super::native::Module, program: &Program, context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool) {
   192	    let (result, unknown, retained, _) = native_observation(rows, schema, module, program, context, ceilings);
   193	    (result, unknown, retained)
   194	}
   195	
   196	#[cfg(feature = "wasm-host")]
   197	pub fn native_observation(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, module: &super::native::Module, program: &Program, mut context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool, super::components::Provenance) {
   198	    if let Err(error) = require_query(program) { return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default()); }
   199	    if let Err(error) = validate_inputs(schema, program, &mut context.args) {
   200	        return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default());
   201	    }
   202	    let args = context.args.clone();
   203	    let now = context.now.unwrap_or(0);
   204	    context.row_provenance |= schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.leave == crate::schema::LeavePolicy::DeliveredHistory);
   205	    let mut runner = Runner::new(rows, schema, context, Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Cap), 0);
   206	    runner.device = true;
   207	    let (value, mut runner) = super::native::run_read(module, runner, &program.name, &args, now);
   208	    let result = (|| {
   209	        let data = match value {
   210	            Ok(data) => data,
   211	            Err(_) if runner.query_unavailable => Value::Null,
   212	            Err(error) => return Err(error.refusal()),
   213	        };
   214	        let data = if runner.query_unavailable { Value::Null } else { data };
   215	        runner.charge_output(&data)?;
   216	        Ok(QueryOutcome { decoration_expiry: runner.decoration_expiry, search_rows: runner.search_rows.take(), search_scopes: None,
   217	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] delivery: None,
   218	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] delivery_meter: None, ephemeral: None,
   219	            unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,
   220	            complete: runner.meter.capped_at.is_none() && runner.word_cut_at.is_none() && !runner.non_uniform && !runner.page_position_lost() && !runner.timeline_pending && !runner.beyond_horizon,
   221	            cut: runner.read_cut(),
   222	            capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
   223	            word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),
   224	            next: None,
   225	            data,
   226	            seq: 0,
   227	            metered: runner.meter.used,
   228	            tables: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect(),
   229	            next_expiry: runner.next_expiry.get(),
   230	        })
   231	    })();
   232	    (result, runner.missing_fact.is_some() || runner.presence_unknown, runner.only_retained_incomplete(), runner.components.provenance())
   233	}

   236	impl Runner<'_> {
   237	    // @ref LLP 3000.016#2.2 — a missing Following card withholds the whole query, including its continuation.
   238	    pub(super) fn withhold_unheld_card(&mut self, table: &str) {
   239	        if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|timeline| table == timeline.posts[0] || table == timeline.reposts[0]) {
   240	            self.query_unavailable = true;
   241	        }
   242	    }
   243	
   244	    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.2 — device-only authority work may prevent
   245	    // prediction, but cannot spend the server-equivalent mutation budget.
   246	    pub(super) fn device_work<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   247	        let Some(allowance) = self.device_allowance.take() else { return work(self) };
   248	        let (caller, entered) = self.enter_device_work(allowance);
   249	        let result = entered.and_then(|_| work(self));
   250	        self.leave_device_work(caller, result.as_ref().err())?;
   251	        result
   252	    }
   253	
   254	    // Shared by every device_work instantiation (wasm size): swap in the
   255	    // device allowance and charge its step; returns the caller's meter.
   256	    #[inline(never)]
   257	    fn enter_device_work(&mut self, mut meter: Meter) -> (Meter, Result<(), RuntimeError>) {
   258	        std::mem::swap(&mut self.meter, &mut meter);
   259	        self.device_work_active = true;
   260	        let step = self.meter.step(1);
   261	        (meter, step)
   262	    }
   263	
   264	    /// Restore the caller's meter; an exhausted allowance cannot refuse the write.
   265	    #[inline(never)]
