The reservation reuses the exported source-write price, so a device consumes the same price the server computes. A null-exempt cap never proves a population bound. Cascade and set null into append-only, field-owned or unpriced children are refused. The postcondition is scoped to the rows present when the delete runs. Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (draft)
     9	**Related:** [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md) (§7, 2026-09-13 "reference IDs have no implicit foreign-key check": this RFC amends its delete half), [LLP 3000.036](./3000.036-what-the-app-farm-asks-of-the-rule-language.rfc.md) (§15.8, the open question this answers; §16.2, the zero-count guard), [LLP 3000.014](./3000.014-a-child-reads-through-its-parent.rfc.md) (§3, a child lives within its parent; §5, predicted parent deletes; §6, `E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN`), [LLP 3000.015](./3000.015-shared-baseline-for-snapback5.spec.md) (§2, one authorization law: work whose shape depends on unreadable rows is charged from a fixed reservation), [LLP 3000.022](./3000.022-delivery-the-sdk-reports.rfc.md) (§14.3, one exported source-write price), [LLP 3000.023](./3000.023-answers-stay-on-screen.rfc.md) (§12, change evidence), [LLP 3000.007](./3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md) (§20.5, held-group proofs for device writes), [LLP 3000.035](./3000.035-quarry-semantics-in-lean.plan.md) (§5.2, the Lean model)
    10	
    11	## Summary
    12	
    13	Deleting a row today leaves every row that references it in place. The
    14	children keep a typed id that names nothing, and reading the parent through
    15	them gives `null`. Wave 5's lane 081 shipped exactly that bug (cancelling a
    16	screening kept its RSVPs), `check` grew a note for it (`N_DELETE_ORPHANS`),
    17	and LLP 3000.036 §15.8 left the design question to the author. The author's
    18	answer: go straight to the end-game.
    19	
    20	A reference column now says what deleting its target does:
    21	
    22	```quarry
    23	table tasks:
    24	  project: projects on delete cascade     -- deleting the project deletes its tasks, in the same commit
    25	  category: categories ? on delete set null   -- deleting the category uncategorizes the task
    26	  owner: principal
    27	  title: text <=200
    28	  cap 500 by project                      -- cascade and set null are bounded by a cap on the reference
    29	  cap 500 by category
    30	  read <- .owner = viewer
    31	  insert <- .owner = viewer
    32	  delete <- .owner = viewer
    33	
    34	table comments:
    35	  task: tasks                              -- undeclared: on delete restrict
    36	  body: text
    37	
    38	table auditLog:
    39	  task: tasks on delete keep               -- history outlives its subject, as every reference did before
    40	  at: time
    41	```
    42	
    43	- **`restrict` is the default.** Deleting a row that a live row still
    44	  references refuses `E_REFERENCED`, naming the referencing column
    45	  (`comments.task`). This is a deliberate behavior change; §8 is the
    46	  migration note, and `check` names every delete site whose outcome it
    47	  changes (`N_DELETE_RESTRICTED`, which replaces `N_DELETE_ORPHANS`).
    48	- **`cascade`** deletes the referencing rows in the same transaction, and
    49	  their own references act in turn. **`set null`** (optional references that
    50	  carry no authority) clears the column. **`keep`** is the old meaning, now
    51	  declared: the row stays and names a deleted row. `cascade` and `set null`
    52	  are authorized by the parent's delete, and only because the schema declares
    53	  them on the child's column.
    54	- **Both writing actions are bounded statically.** They need either
    55	  `cap N by <column>` or a plain, single-column `unique <column>` key, which
    56	  gives that reference an effective bound of one; the delete charges a
    57	  reservation fixed by the schema,
    58	  never by how many children exist; `check` refuses a delete whose
    59	  reservation cannot fit its program's ceilings (`E_CASCADE_BOUND`). There is
    60	  no runtime overflow path and no background sweep (§5.3 says why).
    61	- **What the caller can observe is fixed by the schema**, except the one
    62	  bit `restrict` exists to give: the meter, the touched tables and change
    63	  footprints a commit publishes, the reply's event count and the physical
    64	  authorization allowance never depend on how many (possibly hidden) rows a
    65	  cascade reached (§4.2).
    66	- **A device predicts a parent delete only when it holds every referencing
    67	  row** of the whole closure (the existing held-group proof). Otherwise the
    68	  call queues and the server decides; a predicted delete never predicts half
    69	  its cascade.
    70	
    71	## 1. The problem and the decision being amended
    72	
    73	- **Evidence.** Wave 5 lane 081 (`delete screenings[s]` kept RSVPs; the
    74	  roster listed them and `screeningCard` was null). Wave 6 lanes 029, 032,
    75	  036, 095 and 085 each wrote a zero-count guard or a cleanup loop by hand
    76	  (LLP 3000.036 §16.2). The booking recipe's `removeSlot` exists only to
    77	  refuse while bookings exist. SQL, Prisma, Rails and Django all give a
    78	  per-relation `ON DELETE`; Convex and Firebase give nothing, and their
    79	  users write the cleanup the farm wrote.
    80	- **The decision of 2026-09-13** (LLP 3000 §7) says a reference validates the
    81	  id's value; insert, update and upsert do not read the target; and
    82	  "deleting it neither cascades nor refuses because references remain". This
    83	  RFC replaces the last clause and keeps the rest: **a reference is still not
    84	  an existence check at write time.** A row may be inserted naming an id that
    85	  does not exist, is hidden, or lives in another partition, exactly as today;
    86	  `require exists t[ref] else CODE` remains the explicit form (§4.4 says what
    87	  this leaves open). What changes is what happens to the rows that reference
    88	  a row **at the moment it is deleted**.
    89	
    90	The integrity claim is therefore precise and modest: **when a delete of row
    91	`p` executes, every live row that references `p` at that moment through a
    92	`restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference is refused for, deleted, or
    93	cleared.** It is not "no dangling reference ever exists": a later statement,
    94	even in the same mutation, may insert a row naming `p`, and a `keep`
    95	reference, an excluded reference kind (§2.1) or an expired parent still
    96	leaves the referencing row in place.
    97	
    98	## 2. The form
    99	
   100	```
   101	column: <table> [?] [on delete restrict | on delete cascade | on delete set null | on delete keep] [default …] [written by …]
   102	```
   103	
   104	`on delete` follows the type (and its `?`). One spelling; no `on update`
   105	(ids are immutable).
   106	
   107	### 2.1 Which references carry an action
   108	
   109	A reference **carries an action** when both ends are ordinary durable
   110	tables: the child (the table declaring the column) and the parent (the
   111	table it names) are neither ephemeral nor engine-owned (maintained views,
   112	private maintained state, timeline-owned tables, and a receipt family's
   113	scope, members and runs tables). Every reference that carries an action has
   114	one: the declared one, or `restrict`.
   115	
   116	A reference that does not carry an action keeps today's meaning (the row
   117	stays) and declaring `on delete` on it is `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`:
   118	
   119	| Child or parent | Why no action |
   120	|---|---|
   121	| ephemeral child or parent | ephemeral rows live for seconds and are retired by the engine on its own clock; probing or cascading them would make durable deletes depend on presence |
   122	| engine-owned child or parent | the engine derives or orders these rows; no program writes or deletes them on its own (a receipt scope is deletable only by the system) |
   123	| a field-owned column (`written by`) | its value belongs to its writers' audience, not to the table's rules; probing, clearing or cascading through it would disclose or write a field only its owner may (LLP 3000.007's field authority), so the binder gives it no reference index |
   124	
   125	The integrity of §1 and the migration of §8 therefore cover every reference
   126	**that carries an action**. A field-owned reference keeps today's meaning,
   127	as a reference into an ephemeral table does: it may name a deleted row, and a
   128	read must treat its target as possibly absent.
   129	
   130	### 2.2 Eligibility of each action
   131	
   132	| Action | Requires | Refused |
   133	|---|---|---|
   134	| `restrict` | nothing | — |
   135	| `keep` | nothing | — (no index, no probe, no read gate) |
   136	| `cascade` | `cap N by <column>` on the child (exactly that column), or a plain single-column `unique <column>` key (an inferred effective bound of one) | without either bound: `E_CASCADE_BOUND`. A composite unique key does not bound one reference group. With `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`: a cycle in the cascade graph, including a self-reference, or in the union of cascade and `read through` edges (§3 step 6); a child that is `append only`, has any field-owned (`written by`) column, has a derived synced destination that delivers private fields to their owners, feeds a maintained `sum` (view or column), plays any role in a timeline (owned, mapped or authors), is a row-keyed view's member table (its writes may recount a group outside any fixed price), or whose source writes have no fixed price (a `server_only` reservation plan, LLP 3000.022 §14.3); a `read through` reference whose child can carry a finite effective deadline (§6.1). |
   137	| `set null` | an optional (`?`) reference; either `cap N by <column>` or the same single-column unique inference, whose effective bound is one | everything refused for `cascade` except the cycle rule (set null does not recurse), and a column that **carries authority or meaning anywhere in the schema**: `immutable`, `written by`, a `sequence` parent, the root of a recorded or maintained path (`.column.field`), read by **any** rule of **any** table — the child's own read and write rules (directly or as the first hop of `.column.field`), every other table's `exists`/`created` probe that keys or equates on it, and every rule's hop that passes through it (`.task.column`) — named by the child's `sync` audience or horizon index, or named by any `cap` other than `cap N by <column>` alone. (Another table's sync audience can depend on the column only through a `read through` capture of the child's read rule, which the read-rule exclusion already covers.) |
   138	
   139	Rationale for the `set null` exclusions: each one is a place where the
   140	column's value is more than "which parent this row has". Clearing a column a
   141	rule reads can grant or remove authority (`update <- .assignee = null`, or
   142	another table's `exists grants[document = .id, folder = null]`), and the
   143	parent's deleter was never authorized to change anybody's authority. An
   144	immutable or field-owned column promises nobody else writes it. A recorded
   145	or maintained path stores a fact resolved through the reference. A sync
   146	audience or horizon would move the row between partitions. What remains is
   147	the column that only says where a row is filed (a category, a folder used for
   148	display, a "related to"). A reference the author's rules read chooses
   149	`cascade`, `restrict` or `keep` instead. A self-reference may be `set null`;
   150	it does not recurse.
   151	
   152	**A cap on a `set null` column does not count null.** `cap N by category`
   153	bounds each category's rows; rows whose `category` is null belong to no
   154	parent and are not a group. This is new semantics only for a column that
   155	declares `set null` (a cap on any other nullable column keeps counting its
   156	null group as today), and it is what makes the cap a bound on the
   157	reference's children rather than a limit that the set-null writes would
   158	themselves overflow. Because the null group is then unbounded, **such a cap
   159	never proves a population bound** (a loop's bound, a page's completeness,
   160	mutation admission): those proofs ignore it, as they ignore an index that is
   161	not unique. (A proof that the pinned value is non-null could recover the bound
   162	for one parent's group; §10 records it.) Cap enforcement, activation's group validation, and a device's
   163	cap proofs skip the null group of that column; changing the action away from
   164	`set null` re-validates the cap at activation, null group included.
   165	
   166	The unique inference has the same per-parent scope. It applies to required
   167	and optional references: a plain unique reference has at most one row for each
   168	non-null parent id. An optional unique reference may still have an unbounded
   169	null group. Referential actions probe only a concrete non-null parent id, so
   170	that null group is never counted in the action reservation and the inference
   171	never proves a table population bound. When both declarations exist, the
   172	effective bound is the smaller of the explicit cap and one.
   173	
   174	### 2.3 The reference index
   175	
   176	Every reference whose action probes or writes its children is probed by its
   177	column. The binder reuses a plain index whose leading columns are the
   178	reference (then, for an expiring child, its **effective** deadline column: a
   179	`read through` child's captured `$deadline`, which is the earlier of its own
   180	and its parents' deadlines, else its `expire at` column); otherwise it
   181	synthesizes an engine-named one: `[column, id]`, or
   182	`[column, deadlineColumn, id]` for an expiring child, so one seek skips
   183	an expired backlog (as `read through`'s child index does, LLP 3000.014 §6):
   184	the live rows are exactly `[id, null]` (never expires) and `[id]` with the
   185	deadline after now, so both seeks start at the live suffix and no expired row
   186	is ever visited.
   187	A `read through` reference uses its existing child index. The same index
   188	serves `cap N by <column>`. A `keep` reference gets none.
   189	
   190	## 3. What a delete does
   191	
   192	A delete of row `p` of table `P` — `delete P[id]`, `delete row`, a unique-key
   193	`delete P[key = …]`, a job, `POST /seed`'s delete, or `snapback4 data` —
   194	runs these steps in the deleting transaction, on every host:
   195	
   196	1. **Find and authorize `p`**, as today, with one addition: when any
   197	   `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference names `P`, the caller needs
   198	   **read authority on `p`** as well as delete authority, for every delete
   199	   attempt, with or without children. A caller who may delete but not read
   200	   gets the ordinary hidden-target refusal. This is LLP 3000.014 §3.1's
   201	   rule, generalized from `read through` children to every referenced table,
   202	   and it keeps step 3 from probing a hidden row's children. The system
   203	   principal passes both rules, as it does every rule.
   204	2. **Reserve.** Charge the reservation `R(P)` of §5.1 on every meter, draw
   205	   its row count from the request's physical authorization allowance, and
   206	   publish the schema-fixed trace of §4.2.
   207	3. **Close.** Starting from `p`, follow every `cascade` reference to the
   208	   live rows that reference a reached row, and repeat: the **closure** `S`
   209	   is `p` plus every row reached. (`S` is finite: the cascade graph is
   210	   acyclic and each edge has an explicit or inferred effective bound.) Steps 3–5 stream the referencing rows
   211	   through the reference index (§2.3) a bounded page at a time and keep only
   212	   identities; no image outlives its page.
   213	4. **Restrict.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `restrict` reference
   214	   into `s`'s table, look for a live row that references `s` **and is not
   215	   itself in `S`**: the probe streams past the rows of `S` that name `s` —
   216	   `p` included, which may name itself — to the first live row outside `S`
   217	   (each row of `S` names one target per reference, so a delete's probes
   218	   visit each row of `S` at most once, plus one witness per probe). Every
   219	   such probe runs. If any is occupied, refuse with
   220	   the **first occupied reference in schema order** of
   221	   `(child table, column)` — never the first found while walking hidden
   222	   rows:
   223	
   224	   `E_REFERENCED: projects at <site> is still referenced through comments.task (on delete restrict); delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)`
   225	
   226	   "Live" means present and not expired. A row inserted earlier in the same
   227	   transaction counts; one deleted earlier in it does not. Because rows in
   228	   `S` are excluded, a diamond (`A` cascades to `B` and `C`, and `C`
   229	   restricts `B`) or a self-referencing child table deletes when the whole
   230	   closure goes together, as SQL's statement-end `NO ACTION` does. A `read
   231	   through` reference is not part of this pass: it keeps its own refusal,
   232	   `E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN`, and its stricter physical-child probe (LLP
   233	   3000.014 §3.3), evaluated as each row of `S` is removed in step 6. When
   234	   both would refuse, `E_REFERENCED` comes first (step 4 runs before any
   235	   removal).
   236	5. **Set null.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `set null` reference into
   237	   `s`'s table, clear the column of each live referencing row **not in
   238	   `S`** (deletion dominates: a row that is going away is not rewritten).
   239	   Each reference's group is gathered whole (ids only, at most its effective
   240	   bound: the explicit cap or inferred one)
   241	   before any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling whose
   242	   maintained column shares the reference's index and move it behind a page
   243	   cursor. The write rereads the row's current image immediately before clearing it
   244	   (an earlier clear's maintained write may have changed it), consults no
   245	   rule, and applies its constraints, maintains and partition events as any
   246	   write does.
   247	6. **Delete.** Remove the rows of `S` other than `p`, each table before every
   248	   table it must not outlive: its cascade parents and its `read through`
   249	   parent. Only those edges order the removal (an ordinary `restrict` or
   250	   `set null` reference between rows of `S` imposes none, since step 4
   251	   already cleared them), `check` refuses a cycle in their union
   252	   (`E_REFERENCE_ACTION`; e.g. `B` cascades from `P`, `C` cascades from `B`,
   253	   and `B` reads through `C`), and ties keep discovery order. Each row is
   254	   removed from its current image, consulting no rule and applying
   255	   constraints, maintains and partition events as any delete does. Then
   256	   remove `p` as today, **from its current image too**: the actions may have
   257	   changed it (a maintained column on `p` mirrors its children's removal), and
   258	   a store removes index entries from the image it is given. Authorization
   259	   stays the decision of step 1.
   260	
   261	Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a
   262	`restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and
   263	nothing commits.
   264	
   265	An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
   266	logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
   267	store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
   268	`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
   269	image yet.
   270	
   271	**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
   272	is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
   273	can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
   274	sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
   275	expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
   276	bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
   277	not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
   278	constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
   279	
   280	For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
   281	authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
   282	then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
   283	uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
   284	or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
   285	refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
   286	earlier cascade and set-null writes. An unreadable expired predecessor does not
   287	veto actionable retirement. If the table declares a read-through child, a
   288	writer who cannot read the predecessor receives the insert's ordinary rule
   289	refusal before the engine probes physical child occupancy; that occupancy
   290	cannot disclose a hidden expired identity as a unique constraint.
     1	//! Referential actions: what deleting a referenced row does to the rows that
     2	//! name it (`on delete restrict | cascade | set null`).
     3	// @ref LLP 3000.039#2 — every reference between ordinary durable tables carries one action; restrict is the default.
     4	use super::*;
     5	pub use reservations::Price;
     6	
     7	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
     8	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     9	pub enum OnDelete {
    10	    Restrict,
    11	    Cascade,
    12	    SetNull,
    13	    /// The referencing row stays and names a deleted row (the pre-0.5 meaning),
    14	    /// declared on purpose: history, audit trails, contributions that outlive
    15	    /// their target.
    16	    Keep,
    17	}
    18	
    19	impl OnDelete {
    20	    pub fn words(self) -> &'static str {
    21	        match self { Self::Restrict => "on delete restrict", Self::Cascade => "on delete cascade", Self::SetNull => "on delete set null", Self::Keep => "on delete keep" }
    22	    }
    23	    /// The actions that write the children, bounded by a cap on the reference.
    24	    pub fn writes(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Self::Cascade | Self::SetNull) }
    25	    /// The actions a delete must consult (every one but `keep`).
    26	    pub fn acts(self) -> bool { self != Self::Keep }
    27	}
    28	
    29	/// One action-carrying reference `child.column -> parent`.
    30	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    31	pub struct Referencing<'a> {
    32	    pub child: &'a str,
    33	    pub table: &'a Table,
    34	    pub column: &'a str,
    35	    pub action: OnDelete,
    36	}
    37	
    38	/// The prefix of the reference index a live child of `parent` is found under.
    39	pub const REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX: &str = "$reference:";
    40	pub fn reference_index_name(column: &str) -> String { format!("{REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX}{column}") }
    41	
    42	/// Heap a closure keeps per reached row: its table and id (an id is at most
    43	/// 144 canonical bytes) and the set and queue entries holding them.
    44	pub const CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES: u64 = 384;
    45	/// Child rows a cascade or set-null walk reads per seek (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
    46	pub const REFERENCE_PAGE: usize = 4;
    47	
    48	impl Schema {
    49	    /// Whether rows of `name` take part in referential actions, as child or
    50	    /// parent: an ordinary durable application table. Ephemeral rows, engine
    51	    /// derivations and receipt/timeline bookkeeping keep their own lifetimes.
    52	    pub fn actionable(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
    53	        let Some(table) = self.table(name) else { return false };
    54	        table.ephemeral.is_none() && self.maintain_for(name).is_none() && self.private_owner(name).is_none()
    55	            && !self.is_recount_work(name) && !self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name))
    56	            && !self.receipts.iter().any(|f| [&f.scope, &f.members, &f.runs].iter().any(|t| t.as_str() == name))
    57	    }
    58	
    59	    /// Every reference into `parent` a delete consults (all but `keep`), in
    60	    /// (child, column) order.
    61	    pub fn referencing<'a>(&'a self, parent: &str) -> Vec<Referencing<'a>> {
    62	        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
    63	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    64	        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
    65	            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
    66	                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
    67	                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
    68	                }
    69	            }
    70	        }
    71	        out
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// A delete of a `parent` row consults its referencing rows, so it needs
    75	    /// read authority on that row (LLP 3000.039 §3 step 1).
    76	    pub fn is_referenced(&self, parent: &str) -> bool { !self.referencing(parent).is_empty() }
    77	
    78	    /// The index a reference is probed through: its column first, then the
    79	    /// child's deadline column when the child can expire, so one seek skips an
    80	    /// expired backlog. A `read through` reference uses its child index.
    81	    pub fn reference_index(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    82	        let table = self.table(child)?;
    83	        if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) {
    84	            return table.indexes.contains_key(through::CHILDREN).then_some(through::CHILDREN);
    85	        }
    86	        // The effective deadline: a read-through child's `$deadline`, else `expire at`.
    87	        let deadline = table.expiry_column();
    88	        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| {
    89	            let columns = index.columns();
    90	            index.is_plain() && columns.first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column)
    91	                && deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| columns.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some(deadline))
    92	        }).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    96	    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    97	    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    98	    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    99	    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   100	        let table = self.table(child)?;
   101	        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
   102	            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),

   596	    /// Stop between row removals; a short sweep can still leave due rows.
   597	    pub fn sweep_expired_for(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize, budget: std::time::Duration) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {

   599	        // but commit physical cleanup before attempting a due opening so a
   600	        // refused publication can never wedge the rows whose upper lifetime
   601	        // has already ended.

   606	            }).collect();
   607	        if expiring.is_empty() {
   608	            return Ok(0);
   609	        }

   611	        let now = time_audience::pin_writer_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;

   613	        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
   614	        let mut removed = 0_u64;
   615	        let mut visited = 0_usize;
   616	        let mut expiry_after = self.expiry_after.clone();
   617	        let due = crate::store::Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   618	        let expiring = through_activation::resume_expiry_tables(
   619	            expiring.into_iter().map(|(name, _)| name).collect(), &expiry_after,
   620	        ).into_iter().map(|name| {
   621	            let index = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index().expect("expiring table").0.to_owned();
   622	            (name, index)
   623	        }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   624	        'tables: for (table_name, index) in &expiring {
   625	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   626	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(table_name).cloned();
   627	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   628	            loop {
   629	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   630	                if batch == 0 {
   631	                    break 'tables;
   632	                }

    11	const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";

    13	/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
    14	/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
    15	/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
    16	pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    17	    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    18	    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
    19	) -> Vec<String> {
    20	    let after = cursors
    21	        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
    22	        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
    23	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    24	    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
    25	        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
    26	        tables.rotate_left(next);
    27	    }
    28	    tables
    29	}

    31	pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {

    33	}

    35	/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for
    36	/// existing schemas, including large fixture imports.
    37	pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    38	    schema: &Schema,
    39	    rows: I,
    40	) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
    41	where
    42	    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    43	    I::IntoIter: 'a,
    44	{
    45	    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {
    46	        return Box::new(rows.into_iter());
    47	    }
    48	    let order = schema.through_order();
    49	    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    50	    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
    51	    Box::new(rows.into_iter())
    52	}

    64	fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    65	    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {
    66	        let mut end = text.len().min(256);
    67	        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
    68	            end -= 1;
    69	        }
    70	        &text[..end]
    71	    }
    72	    if samples.len() < 5 {
    73	        let id = row
    74	            .field("id")
    75	            .ok()
    76	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    77	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
    78	        let value = row
    79	            .field(reference)
    80	            .ok()
    81	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    82	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
    83	        samples.push(format!(
    84	            "{}: {reference} -> {parent}[{}]",
    85	            bounded(id),
    86	            bounded(value)
    87	        ));
    88	    }
    89	}

    91	fn rows(

   109	fn correspondence(
   110	    child: &RuleExpr,
   111	    parent: &RuleExpr,
   112	) -> Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>> {
   113	    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
   114	        return Some(Default::default());
   115	    }
   116	    fn walk(
   117	        a: &serde_json::Value,
   118	        b: &serde_json::Value,
   119	        map: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
   120	    ) -> bool {
   121	        use serde_json::Value::*;
   122	        match (a, b) {
   123	            (Object(a), Object(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   124	                if let (Some(String(a)), Some(String(b))) = (a.get("Field"), b.get("Field")) {
   125	                    if map.get(a).is_some_and(|old| old != b)
   126	                        || map.iter().any(|(old, v)| v == b && old != a)
   127	                    {
   128	                        return false;
   129	                    }
   130	                    map.insert(a.clone(), b.clone());
   131	                    true
   132	                } else {
   133	                    a.iter()
   134	                        .all(|(k, a)| b.get(k).is_some_and(|b| walk(a, b, map)))
   135	                }
   136	            }
   137	            (Array(a), Array(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   138	                a.iter().zip(b).all(|(a, b)| walk(a, b, map))
   139	            }
   140	            _ => a == b,
   141	        }
   142	    }
   143	    let mut map = Default::default();
   144	    walk(
   145	        &serde_json::to_value(child).ok()?,
   146	        &serde_json::to_value(parent).ok()?,
   147	        &mut map,
   148	    )
   149	    .then_some(map)
   150	}

   152	/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
   153	/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
   154	/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
   155	pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
   156	    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
   157	    now: i64,
   158	}
   159	
   160	impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
   161	    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
   162	        let affected = next
   163	            .through_order()
   164	            .into_iter()
   165	            .filter_map(|name| {
   166	                let next = &next.tables[&name];
   167	                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
   168	                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
   169	            })
   170	            .collect();
   171	        Self { affected, now }
   172	    }
   173	
   174	    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
   175	        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
   176	    }
   177	
   178	    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
   179	        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
   180	    }
   181	
   182	    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
   183	        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
   187	        self.affected
   188	            .iter()
   189	            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
   190	            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
   191	    }
   192	}

+Prediction also runs commit-end retirement for every row the mutation inserts
+or updates into an already-expired final image, before final-exists clauses.
+With complete reference-group coverage it publishes the same cascade and
+set-null changes or the same restrict refusal as the server. Missing coverage,
+retained history or another uncertain witness queues the whole mutation with
+no predicted rows. An unreferenced expiring row still retires locally at commit
+end; expiry alone does not force an otherwise provable mutation online. The
+retirement and its schema-fixed action reservation draw from the device's
+separate bounded physical-work allowance. Exhausting it queues and rolls back
+the prediction; it cannot publish a partial closure or become a server refusal.
+
 Any schema in which an expiring table is referenced requires device capability
 `expiry-reference-actions-v1`. A pre-Wave-12 stored schema may open on the
 server for transactional adoption and is restamped when published, but an old

         let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));

+        let work = meter.map(|meter| std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used).unwrap_or_default();
         retired.map(|()| work)
     }

+    // Commit-end retirement is part of device prediction too. With complete
+    // public coverage, updating a parent to an already-ended lifetime applies
+    // the same cascade and set-null closure as the server. A child born earlier
+    // in the same mutation belongs to that closure as well.
+    let predicted_expiry = r#"
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  parent: parents on delete restrict
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+mutation expire(parent: parents):
+  update parents[parent] { until: now }
+  insert cascadeKids { id: 'born', parent }
+"#;
+    let row = |table: &str, fields: &[(&str, snapback4_core::Value)]|
+        (table.to_owned(), snapback4_core::value::object(fields.iter().cloned()));
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(predicted_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([
+        row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))]),
+        row("cascadeKids", &[("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("nullableKids", &[("id", id("nullable")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-actions", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let predicted = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty(), "the old and same-mutation children cascade");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-actions", d);
+
+    // The device charges the schema's worst-case closure before walking it.
+    // A large declared cap therefore queues even when this particular store
+    // contains only the child this mutation just inserted; no unbounded
+    // commit-end walk can escape the prediction allowance.
+    let bounded_expiry = predicted_expiry.replace("cap 4 by parent", "cap 1024 by parent");
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(&bounded_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))])], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-bounded", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let queued = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(queued.code(), "E_PREDICT", "{}: {queued:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("parents")[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty(), "queued prediction rolls back its new child");
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap().is_empty());
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-bounded", d);
+
+    // A complete restrict witness refuses locally and rolls back the parent
+    // update plus the child inserted before commit-end retirement.
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(predicted_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([
+        row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))]),
+        row("cascadeKids", &[("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("nullableKids", &[("id", id("nullable")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("blockers", &[("id", id("blocker")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-restrict", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let refused = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refused.code(), "E_REFERENCED", "{}: {refused:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("parents")[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").len(), 1, "the same-mutation child rolls back");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &id("p"));
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "E_REFERENCED");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap()[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-restrict", d);
+
+    // Expiry itself does not force an online round trip. An unreferenced row
+    // can be updated or born already expired and disappear in the prediction.
+    let plain_expiry = r#"
+table notes:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation expire(note: notes):
+  update notes[note] { until: now }
+mutation createExpired():
+  insert notes { id: 'born', until: now }
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(plain_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([row("notes", &[("id", id("note")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))])], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-plain-expiry", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let predicted = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"note":"note"}), 100, vec![], 1);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("notes").is_empty());
+    d.withdraw(&[]).unwrap();
+    let predicted = d.predict("createExpired", "alice", &json!({}), 100, vec![], 2);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("notes").len(), 1, "withdrawing the first prediction restores its live base row");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("notes")[0].field("id").unwrap(), &id("note"));
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("note", id("note"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("notes").unwrap().is_empty());
+    host.close("predicted-plain-expiry", d);
+
     // An expiring row-keyed-view source follows the same server action path;
     // derived maintenance cannot delete it before cascade/set-null run. The
     // device receives the committed source and child changes together.

commit ee824cac6fdb5cbd0810d5298af6072018bba5b7
Author:     Charlie Cheever <ccheever@firewoodagent.com>
AuthorDate: Thu Oct 15 03:48:13 2026 +0200
Commit:     Charlie Cheever <ccheever@firewoodagent.com>
CommitDate: Thu Oct 15 03:48:13 2026 +0200

    Generate device expiry action parity cases
---
 .../tests/wave12_expiry_actions_generated.rs       | 646 +++++++++++++++++++++
 .../raw/generated-device-expiry.log.gz             | Bin 0 -> 1554 bytes
 .../wave12-lang/r13-expiry-generation/receipt.json |  47 ++
 3 files changed, 693 insertions(+)

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-difftest/tests/wave12_expiry_actions_generated.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-difftest/tests/wave12_expiry_actions_generated.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..8fea760f4c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-difftest/tests/wave12_expiry_actions_generated.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,646 @@
+//! Generated device/server parity for commit-end lifetime retirement. Each
+//! source runs through the public sync wire and both device stores, so an
+//! offline prediction cannot silently omit a cascade, set-null or restrict
+//! action performed by the server.
+
+#[path = "../../snapback4-device/tests/common/mod.rs"]
+mod device_common;
+
+use device_common::{
+    BoundaryMetadata, Host, Memory, Sqlite, args, compile, id, snapshot_pages, stream_page,
+};
+use serde_json::json;
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
+use snapback4_device::device::Device;
+
+const NOW: i64 = 4_000_000_000_000;
+const GENERATED_SOURCES: usize = 18;
+const GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES: usize = 9;
+const RUNTIME_CASES: usize = GENERATED_SOURCES * 2;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Action {
+    Cascade,
+    SetNull,
+    Restrict,
+}
+
+impl Action {
+    fn word(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Cascade => "cascade",
+            Self::SetNull => "set null",
+            Self::Restrict => "restrict",
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn optional(self) -> &'static str {
+        if matches!(self, Self::SetNull) {
+            " ?"
+        } else {
+            ""
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Prelude {
+    Snapshot,
+    Stream,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Target {
+    ExpiredWithInbound,
+    FutureWithInbound,
+    ExpiredWithoutInbound,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum IncompleteCoverage {
+    MissingChild,
+    AudienceHidden,
+    PartiallyAcquired,
+}
+
+impl Target {
+    fn has_inbound(self) -> bool {
+        !matches!(self, Self::ExpiredWithoutInbound)
+    }
+
+    fn requested_expiry(self) -> i64 {
+        if matches!(self, Self::FutureWithInbound) {
+            NOW + 10_000
+        } else {
+            NOW
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+struct Generated {
+    seed: u64,
+    action: Action,
+    prelude: Prelude,
+    target: Target,
+    viewer: &'static str,
+    decoys: usize,
+    source: String,
+}
+
+fn generated_sources() -> Vec<Generated> {
+    let mut generated = Vec::new();
+    let mut seed = 0_u64;
+    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
+        for target in [
+            Target::ExpiredWithInbound,
+            Target::FutureWithInbound,
+            Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound,
+        ] {
+            for prelude in [Prelude::Snapshot, Prelude::Stream] {
+                let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
+                let decoys = 1 + (seed as usize % 2);
+                let cap = decoys + 2;
+                let source = format!(
+                    r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  token: int
+  expire at .until
+  public 'generated expiry parents seed {seed}'
+  insert <- allow
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
+  marker: int
+  cap {cap} by parent
+  public 'generated expiry children seed {seed}'
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation addChild(id: id, parent: parents, marker: int):
+  insert children {{ id, parent, marker }}
+mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
+  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
+"#,
+                    optional = action.optional(),
+                    action = action.word(),
+                );
+                generated.push(Generated {
+                    seed,
+                    action,
+                    prelude,
+                    target,
+                    viewer,
+                    decoys,
+                    source,
+                });
+                seed += 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(generated.len(), GENERATED_SOURCES);
+    generated
+}
+
+fn row(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'static str, Value)>) -> Value {
+    snapback4_core::value::object(fields)
+}
+
+fn target_parent() -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id("target")),
+        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000)),
+        ("token", Value::Int(7)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn target_child(seed: u64) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id("target-child")),
+        ("parent", id("target")),
+        ("marker", Value::Int(seed as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn decoy_parent(index: usize) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
+        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 20_000 + index as i64)),
+        ("token", Value::Int(100 + index as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn decoy_child(index: usize) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-child-{index}"))),
+        ("parent", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
+        ("marker", Value::Int(200 + index as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn seed_rows(case: &Generated) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
+    let mut rows = vec![("parents".to_owned(), target_parent())];
+    for index in 0..case.decoys {
+        rows.push(("parents".to_owned(), decoy_parent(index)));
+        let streamed_decoy =
+            matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) && !case.target.has_inbound() && index == 0;
+        if !streamed_decoy {
+            rows.push(("children".to_owned(), decoy_child(index)));
+        }
+    }
+    if case.target.has_inbound() && matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Snapshot) {
+        rows.push(("children".to_owned(), target_child(case.seed)));
+    }
+    rows
+}
+
+fn canonical(rows: Vec<Value>) -> Vec<String> {
+    let mut rows = rows
+        .into_iter()
+        .map(|row| {
+            let mut row = snapback4_core::wire::to_json(&row);
+            // `pending` is device settlement metadata, not an authored field;
+            // parity below compares the predicted data image with the server's
+            // committed data image.
+            if let Some(object) = row.as_object_mut() {
+                object.remove("pending");
+            }
+            serde_json::to_string(&row).unwrap()
+        })
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    rows.sort();
+    rows
+}
+
+fn device_rows<S: BoundaryMetadata>(device: &Device<S>, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
+    device.store().raw_rows(table)
+}
+
+fn server_rows(server: &Engine, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
+    server.store().rows(table).unwrap()
+}
+
+fn row_by_id<'a>(rows: &'a [Value], wanted: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
+    rows.iter()
+        .find(|row| row.field("id").ok() == Some(&id(wanted)))
+}
+
+fn apply_snapshot<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    device: &mut Device<S>,
+    viewer: &str,
+) -> (u64, usize) {
+    let pages = snapshot_pages(server, viewer, 2);
+    let watermark = pages.last().expect("a snapshot has a final page").watermark;
+    for (index, page) in pages.iter().enumerate() {
+        device.apply(page, index == 0).unwrap();
+    }
+    (watermark, pages.len())
+}
+
+fn server_write(
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    op: &str,
+    viewer: &str,
+    values: &[(&str, Value)],
+    now: i64,
+) -> Result<(), String> {
+    let outcome = server
+        .mutate(op, None, Context::new(viewer, args(values)).at(now))
+        .unwrap();
+    match outcome.state {
+        WriteState::Sent { .. } => Ok(()),
+        WriteState::Failed { why, .. } => Err(why.code),
+    }
+}
+
+fn prelude<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
+    case: &Generated,
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    device: &mut Device<S>,
+) -> (usize, usize) {
+    let (watermark, snapshot_count) = apply_snapshot(server, device, case.viewer);
+    let mut stream_count = 0;
+    if matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) {
+        let (child, parent, marker) = if case.target.has_inbound() {
+            (
+                "target-child".to_owned(),
+                "target".to_owned(),
+                case.seed as i64,
+            )
+        } else {
+            ("decoy-child-0".to_owned(), "decoy-parent-0".to_owned(), 200)
+        };
+        server_write(
+            server,
+            "addChild",
+            case.viewer,
+            &[
+                ("id", id(&child)),
+                ("parent", id(&parent)),
+                ("marker", Value::Int(marker)),
+            ],
+            NOW - 1,
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+        device
+            .apply(&stream_page(server, case.viewer, watermark), false)
+            .unwrap();
+        stream_count += 1;
+    }
+
+    for table in ["parents", "children"] {
+        assert_eq!(
+            canonical(device_rows(device, table)),
+            canonical(server_rows(server, table)),
+            "seed {} {:?}/{:?}: prelude sync differs for {table}",
+            case.seed,
+            case.action,
+            case.prelude,
+        );
+    }
+    (snapshot_count, stream_count)
+}
+
+fn assert_expected<S: BoundaryMetadata>(case: &Generated, server: &Engine, device: &Device<S>) {
+    let device_parents = device_rows(device, "parents");
+    let device_children = device_rows(device, "children");
+    let server_parents = server_rows(server, "parents");
+    let server_children = server_rows(server, "children");
+    let label = format!(
+        "seed {} {:?}/{:?}/{:?}",
+        case.seed, case.action, case.target, case.prelude
+    );
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_parents.clone()),
+        canonical(server_parents.clone()),
+        "{label}: parent parity"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_children.clone()),
+        canonical(server_children.clone()),
+        "{label}: child parity"
+    );
+
+    let target_parent = row_by_id(&device_parents, "target");
+    let target_child = row_by_id(&device_children, "target-child");
+    match (case.action, case.target) {
+        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            let parent = target_parent.expect("restrict refusal preserves its parent");
+            assert_eq!(
+                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
+                &Value::Int(NOW + 5_000),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&id("target")),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (_, Target::FutureWithInbound) => {
+            let parent = target_parent.expect("future expiry preserves its parent");
+            assert_eq!(
+                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
+                &Value::Int(NOW + 10_000),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&id("target")),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (Action::Cascade, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
+            assert!(target_child.is_none(), "{label}: cascade retires the child");
+        }
+        (Action::SetNull, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&Value::Null),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (_, Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound) => {
+            assert!(
+                target_parent.is_none(),
+                "{label}: an unreferenced expired parent retires"
+            );
+            assert!(
+                target_child.is_none(),
+                "{label}: the source generated no inbound reference"
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    let target_remains = matches!(case.target, Target::FutureWithInbound)
+        || matches!(
+            (case.action, case.target),
+            (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
+        );
+    assert_eq!(
+        device_parents.len(),
+        case.decoys + if target_remains { 1 } else { 0 },
+        "{label}: every decoy parent remains and only the expected target image survives"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        device_children
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|row| row.field("id").ok() != Some(&id("target-child")))
+            .count(),
+        case.decoys,
+        "{label}: every unrelated child remains",
+    );
+}
+
+fn run_case<H: Host>(host: &mut H, case: &Generated) -> (usize, usize) {
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&case.source);
+    server.seed_at(seed_rows(case), NOW - 100).unwrap();
+    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-generated-{}", case.seed);
+    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    let counts = prelude(case, &mut server, &mut device);
+    let input = json!({"parent":"target", "until":case.target.requested_expiry()});
+    let predicted = device.predict("setExpiry", case.viewer, &input, NOW, vec![], 1);
+    let committed = server_write(
+        &mut server,
+        "setExpiry",
+        case.viewer,
+        &[
+            ("parent", id("target")),
+            ("until", Value::Int(case.target.requested_expiry())),
+        ],
+        NOW,
+    );
+
+    if matches!(
+        (case.action, case.target),
+        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
+    ) {
+        assert_eq!(
+            predicted.unwrap_err().code(),
+            "E_REFERENCED",
+            "seed {} {}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            committed.unwrap_err(),
+            "E_REFERENCED",
+            "seed {} {}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+    } else {
+        assert!(
+            predicted.is_ok(),
+            "seed {} {}: {predicted:?}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {} {}", case.seed, host.label());
+    }
+    assert_expected(case, &server, &device);
+    host.close(&store_name, device);
+    counts
+}
+
+fn incomplete_source(seed: u64, action: Action) -> String {
+    let cap = 3 + seed as usize % 2;
+    format!(
+        r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public 'incomplete expiry parents seed {seed}'
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
+  owner: principal
+  cap {cap} by parent
+  read <- .owner = viewer
+  insert <- .owner = viewer
+  sync to .owner
+mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
+  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
+"#,
+        optional = action.optional(),
+        action = action.word(),
+    )
+}
+
+fn incomplete_rows(mode: IncompleteCoverage, viewer: &str) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
+    let mut rows = vec![(
+        "parents".to_owned(),
+        row([("id", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000))]),
+    )];
+    let hidden = if viewer == "alice" { "bob" } else { "alice" };
+    if matches!(
+        mode,
+        IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden | IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired
+    ) {
+        rows.push((
+            "children".to_owned(),
+            row([
+                ("id", id("hidden")),
+                ("parent", id("target")),
+                ("owner", id(hidden)),
+            ]),
+        ));
+    }
+    if matches!(mode, IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired) {
+        rows.push((
+            "children".to_owned(),
+            row([
+                ("id", id("visible")),
+                ("parent", id("target")),
+                ("owner", id(viewer)),
+            ]),
+        ));
+    }
+    rows
+}
+
+fn run_incomplete_case<H: Host>(
+    host: &mut H,
+    seed: u64,
+    action: Action,
+    mode: IncompleteCoverage,
+) -> usize {
+    let source = incomplete_source(seed, action);
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&source);
+    let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
+    server
+        .seed_at(incomplete_rows(mode, viewer), NOW - 100)
+        .unwrap();
+    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-incomplete-{seed}");
+    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    let (_, pages) = apply_snapshot(&mut server, &mut device, viewer);
+    let parents_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents"));
+    let children_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "children"));
+
+    let predicted = device
+        .predict(
+            "setExpiry",
+            viewer,
+            &json!({"parent":"target", "until":NOW}),
+            NOW,
+            vec![],
+            1,
+        )
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(
+        predicted.code(),
+        "E_PREDICT",
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?} {} must queue an unprovable action group",
+        host.label()
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents")),
+        parents_before,
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no parent"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_rows(&device, "children")),
+        children_before,
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no visible child"
+    );
+
+    let committed = server_write(
+        &mut server,
+        "setExpiry",
+        viewer,
+        &[("parent", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW))],
+        NOW,
+    );
+    let has_child = mode != IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild;
+    if matches!(action, Action::Restrict) && has_child {
+        assert_eq!(
+            committed,
+            Err("E_REFERENCED".to_owned()),
+            "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
+        );
+        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_some());
+    } else {
+        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}");
+        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_none());
+        let children = server_rows(&server, "children");
+        match action {
+            Action::Cascade => assert!(children.is_empty(), "seed {seed} {mode:?}"),
+            Action::SetNull => assert!(
+                children
+                    .iter()
+                    .all(|row| row.field("parent").ok() == Some(&Value::Null)),
+                "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
+            ),
+            Action::Restrict => assert!(
+                children.is_empty(),
+                "the missing-child control has no child"
+            ),
+        }
+    }
+    host.close(&store_name, device);
+    pages
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn generated_commit_end_expiry_actions_match_server_on_both_device_stores() {
+    let generated = generated_sources();
+    let mut memory = Memory::new();
+    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-generated");
+    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
+    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
+    let mut stream_pages_seen = 0;
+    for case in &generated {
+        for counts in [run_case(&mut memory, case), run_case(&mut sqlite, case)] {
+            runtime_cases += 1;
+            snapshot_pages_seen += counts.0;
+            stream_pages_seen += counts.1;
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, RUNTIME_CASES);
+    assert_eq!(
+        stream_pages_seen, 18,
+        "nine stream-prelude sources run on two stores"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases,
+        "every runtime starts from a real public-sync snapshot"
+    );
+    println!(
+        "generated {GENERATED_SOURCES} sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; {stream_pages_seen} prelude stream pages; 72 independently asserted target outcomes"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn generated_incomplete_action_groups_queue_without_predicted_rows() {
+    let mut memory = Memory::new();
+    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-incomplete");
+    let mut seed = 100_u64;
+    let mut sources = 0;
+    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
+    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
+    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
+        for mode in [
+            IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild,
+            IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden,
+            IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired,
+        ] {
+            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut memory, seed, action, mode);
+            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut sqlite, seed, action, mode);
+            sources += 1;
+            runtime_cases += 2;
+            seed += 1;
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(sources, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES);
+    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES * 2);
+    assert!(snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases);
+    println!(
+        "generated {sources} incomplete-coverage sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite queue cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; all 18 device outcomes were exact E_PREDICT with zero local changes"
+    );
+}

   222	    pub fn replay(&mut self, viewer: &str, op: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {

   231	    fn replay_mutation(&mut self, viewer: &str, id: &str, name: &str, args_digest: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
   232	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   233	        let receipt = tx.applied_bound(viewer, id, name, args_digest)?;
   234	        tx.rollback()?;

   238	    pub fn mutate(&mut self, name: &str, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {
   239	        context.generation = self.generation();
   240	        let wire_args = if op.is_some() { context.wire_args.take().unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::Value::Object(crate::wire::map_to_json(&context.args))) }
   241	            else { serde_json::Value::Null };
   242	        let args_digest = crate::store::payload_digest(&wire_args);
   243	        // Preserve the bound replay-before-validation contract, including
   244	        // unknown or renamed programs. Never return a historical result row.
   245	        if let Some(op) = op
   246	            && let Some(outcome) = self.replay_mutation(&context.viewer, op, name, &args_digest)?
   247	        {
   248	            return Ok(outcome);
   249	        }
   250	        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
   251	            self.schema.check_delivery(name, context.delivery_fingerprint.as_deref()).err()
   252	                .unwrap_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))
   253	        })?.clone();
   254	        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
   255	        if context.entropy == 0 {
   256	            context.entropy = crate::ids::seed();
   257	        }
   258	        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — retries rerun Quarry, rules, maintains, and bookkeeping together

   260	            match self.mutate_once(&program, op, context.clone(), &args_digest) {
   261	                Err(error) if retry_transaction(&error) && attempt < 32 => {
   262	                    self.retries += 1;
   263	                    let delay = (100_u64 << attempt.min(6)) + crate::ids::seed() % 250;
   264	                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_micros(delay));
   265	                }
   266	                outcome => return outcome,
   267	            }
   268	        }
   269	        unreachable!()
   270	    }

     2	use super::store::Tx;
     3	use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{adoption, word_heap as heap}, schema::{IndexComponent, Schema, Table}, value::{Value, canonical_json}};

     5	pub(super) fn install(tx: &Tx<'_>, schema: &mut Schema) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
     6	    let backend = tx.query("SELECT schema,generation FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
     7	    let previous: Schema = super::store::decode(backend[0].get(0))?;
     8	    let mut generation = backend[0].get::<_, i64>(1);
     9	    schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
    10	    if *schema != previous {
    11	        for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
    12	            for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
    13	                let Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() else {continue};
    14	                if previous.table(name).and_then(|t|t.index(index_name)) == Some(index) {continue;}
    15	                tx.execute("DELETE FROM i WHERE t = $1 AND ix = $2", &[name,index_name])?;
    16	                let work=adoption::Work::DECODE.with_contribution(maintain);
    17	                let mut after: Option<String> = None;
    18	                loop {
    19	                    let mut meter=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);
    20	                    meter.at(&format!("adopt {name}.{index_name}"));
    21	                    meter.heap(4096 + after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
    22	                    let page=source_page(&tx,name,table,after.as_deref(),&mut meter,work)?;
    23	                    if page.is_empty() { break; }
    24	                    for raw in &page {
    25	                        let scratch=meter.mark();
    26	                        let id=raw.get::<_,&str>(0);
    27	                        let data=raw.get::<_,&str>(1);
    28	                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
    29	                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
    30	                        let row: Value=super::store::decode(data)?;
    31	                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
    32	                        meter.step(maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
    33	                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::contribution_bytes(&row,table))?;
    34	                        for key in crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table,index,&row,id) {
    35	                            if key.len() > crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES { return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(name,index_name,1)); }
    36	                            meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries,1)?;
    37	                            tx.execute("INSERT INTO i(t,ix,k,id) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)", &[name,index_name,&key,&id])?;
    38	                        }
    39	                        drop(row);
    40	                        meter.release_heap(scratch);
    41	                    }
    42	                    let last=page.last().expect("nonempty page").get::<_,&str>(0);
    43	                    meter.heap(heap::text(last))?;
    44	                    after=Some(last.to_owned());
    45	                    // The full driver-owned page remains reserved until every
    46	                    // decoded row and its index scratch have been consumed.
    47	                    drop(page);
    48	                }
    49	            }
    50	        }
    51	        generation=generation.checked_add(1).ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?;
    52	        tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET schema = $1, generation = $2 WHERE singleton", &[&canonical_json(schema), &generation])?;
    53	    }
    54	    u64::try_from(generation).map_err(|_|RuntimeError::Generation("negative generation".into()))
    55	}

    57	// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9.3 — adoption reserves fetched images separately from per-row contribution scratch.
    58	pub(super) fn source_page(tx: &super::store::Tx<'_>, table: &str, schema: &Table, after: Option<&str>, meter: &mut Meter, work: adoption::Work) -> Result<Vec<postgres::Row>, RuntimeError> {
    59	    let sizes=if after.is_some() {
    60	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    61	    } else {
    62	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    63	    };
    64	    let mut limit=32i64;
    65	    let page_mark=meter.mark();
    66	    loop {
    67	        limit=work.limit(meter,limit as usize) as i64;
    68	        let size=tx.query(sizes,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    69	        let bytes=size[0].get::<_,i64>(0) as u64;
    70	        let count=size[0].get::<_,i64>(1) as u64;
    71	        // Network/read buffers, retained driver rows and their metadata. Typed
    72	        // JSON decode is priced from borrowed text later, one row at a time;
    73	        // the query scan's conservative 256x all-rows decoder is inappropriate
    74	        // for this walk. This initial estimate is followed by a scratch check
    75	        // before any adoption callback runs.
    76	        let reservation=bytes.saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(count.saturating_mul(1024));
    77	        if limit>1 && reservation>meter.ceilings.heap_bytes/2 { limit/=2; continue; }
    78	        meter.heap(reservation)?;
    79	        let query=if after.is_some() {
    80	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    81	        } else {
    82	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    83	        };
    84	        let page=tx.query(query,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    85	        if adoption::page_fits(page.iter().map(|raw| raw.get::<_,&str>(1)), meter, work,
    86	            Some(&|row| adoption::contribution_bytes(row,schema)))? { return Ok(page); }
    87	        limit=(page.len() as i64/2).max(1);
    88	        drop(page);
    89	        meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
    90	    }
    91	}

   111	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   112	    match kind {
   113	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   114	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   115	        _ => false,
   116	    }
   117	}
   118	
   119	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   120	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   121	    match rule {
   122	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   123	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   124	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   125	        _ => false,
   126	    }
   127	}
   128	
   129	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   130	    match rule {
   131	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   132	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   133	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   134	        _ => false,
   135	    }
   136	}

   138	impl Schema {
   139	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   140	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   141	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   142	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   143	    }
   144	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   145	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   146	    }
   147	}

     3	/-!
     4	# Writes: rule checks and refusals
     5	
     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
     7	writes card:
     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
    10	  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
    25	  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
    26	  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
    27	  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
    28	  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
    29	  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).
    30	
    31	The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the
    32	model's order is OPEN W1–W6.

    37	def notFound : Stop := .refuse "NOT_FOUND"
    38	def eRule : Stop := .refuse "E_RULE"
    39	def eInput : Stop := .refuse "E_INPUT"
    40	
    41	def toScalarE : Value → Except Stop Scalar
    42	  | .s x => pure x
    43	  | _ => throw eInput
    44	
    45	def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    46	  fs.mapM fun p => do return (p.1, ← toScalarE p.2)
    47	
    48	/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
    49	def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null
    50	
    51	/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
    52	required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))
    54	    (missing : Stop) : Except Stop Row := do
    55	  if fields.any fun p => p.1 != "id" && !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    56	  let cols ← td.cols.mapM fun c => match fields.lookup c.name with
    57	    | some x => if fits c x then pure (c.name, x) else throw eInput
    58	    | none => if c.nullable then pure (c.name, Scalar.null) else throw missing
    59	  return { id := rid, cols }
    60	
    61	/-- The next image of an update: the patch replaces named columns. -/
    62	def patchImage (td : TableDecl) (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop Row := do
    63	  if patch.any fun p => !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput

    65	    | some x =>

    67	      | some c => if fits c x then pure (p.1, x) else throw eInput
    68	      | none => throw eInput
    69	    | none => pure p

    71	
    72	def keyOf (cols : List String) (r : Row) : List (String × Scalar) := cols.map fun c => (c, r.get c)
    73	
    74	/-- The first unique key (in order) on which another row (not `except`)
    75	collides with `img`. Keys with a null component never collide (a nullable
    76	unique key permits tied nulls; indexes card). -/
    77	def findClash (rows : List Row) (keys : List (List String)) (img : Row) (except : Option (List Nat)) :
    78	    Option (Nat × Row) :=
    79	  let rec go (i : Nat) : List (List String) → Option (Nat × Row)
    80	    | [] => none

    82	      let kv := keyOf k img
    83	      if kv.any (·.2 == .null) then go (i + 1) ks
