    85	        | some r => some (i, r)
    86	        | none => go (i + 1) ks

    88	
    89	/-- The refusal for a visible clash on unique key `i` of `["id"] ++ uniques`
    90	(`withId`) or of `uniques`. -/
    91	def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
    92	  let j := if withId then i - 1 else i
    93	  if withId && i = 0 then .refuse "E_CONSTRAINT"

    95	    | some (some code) => .refuse code
    96	    | _ => .refuse "E_UNIQUE"

    98	def findRow (rows : List Row) (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
    99	  if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)

   101	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#7 — expired rows release every logical lookup key.
   102	/-- A write target lookup selects among live rows, rather than selecting a
   103	physical predecessor and rejecting it after it has hidden a live match. -/
   104	def findLiveRow (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (rows : List Row)

   110	def resultOf (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   111	  if readable sch s v t r then r.toValue else .null
   112	
   113	def resultOfAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   114	    (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   115	  if readableAt sch s v now t r then r.toValue else .null
   116	
   117	/-- `guardE b e` continues when `b` holds and refuses `e` otherwise. -/
   118	def guardE (b : Bool) (e : Stop) : Except Stop Unit := if b then .ok () else .error e
   119	
   120	def doInsertImage (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   121	    (img : Row) (clashHidden : Stop) :
   122	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   123	  -- Insert authority has already been checked. Remaining unique checks and
   124	  -- the physical insertion use the post-retirement store.

   133	/-- An update's `if` condition: `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable target,
   134	`E_CONFLICT` when false. -/
   135	def condCheck (rd : Bool) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) (old : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   136	  match cond with

   138	    guardE rd notFound
   139	    let b ← f old

   174	/-! ## Referential actions (LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   175	
   176	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
   177	`(child table, column, action)`. -/
   178	def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=
   179	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => td.cols.filterMap fun c =>
   180	    match c.ref, c.onDelete with
   181	    | some p, some a => if p == t then some (td.name, c.name, a) else none
   182	    | _, _ => none

   184	/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
   185	def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i
   186	
   187	def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   188	  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id
   189	
   190	/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
   191	def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
   192	  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
   193	    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []
   194	
   195	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
   196	bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
   197	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
   198	  | 0, _, acc => acc
   199	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
   200	  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
   201	    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
   202	    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)
   203	
   204	/-- Some `restrict` reference names a closure row from outside the closure. -/
   205	def restricted (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (cl : List (String × Row)) : Bool :=
   206	  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
   207	    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k
   208	
   209	def clearCol (r : Row) (c : String) : Row :=
   210	  { r with cols := r.cols.map fun p => if p.1 == c then (p.1, Scalar.null) else p }
   211	
   212	/-- Clear every `set null` reference that names a closure row from outside it. -/
   213	def setNulls (sch : Schema) (cl : List (String × Row)) (s : Store) : Store :=
   214	  cl.foldl (fun s (t, r) => (referencing sch t).foldl (fun s (c, col, a) =>
   215	    if a == .setNull then
   216	      ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k).foldl
   217	        (fun s k => s.replaceRow c k (clearCol k col)) s
   218	    else s) s) s
   219	
   220	def storeSize (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat := sch.tables.foldl (fun n td => n + (s td.name).length) 0
   221	
   222	/-- The store after deleting `old` from `t` with its referential actions, or
   223	`E_REFERENCED`. With no action-carrying reference into `t`, exactly
   224	`removeRow` (LLP 3000.039 §1). -/
   225	def refDelete (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=

   232	def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=

   260	transaction as the insert. -/

+### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
+
+Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
+64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
+`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
+The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
+identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
+adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
+address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
+
+The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
+aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
+marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
+of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
+target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
+generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
+together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
+are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
+it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
+zero.
+

-**Expiry is not a delete.** A parent whose `expire at` passes is absent from
-that moment, and the sweep removes it physically; neither fires an action.
-A child of an expiring parent outlives it unless the child declares the same
-lifetime (`read through`, or its own `expire at`). The writes card says so.
+**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
+is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
+can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
+sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
+expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
+bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
+not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
+constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
+
+A live `restrict` child keeps the expired root physically stored and the sweep
+continues to later due keys. The retained root remains logically unreadable.
+Short sweeps preserve a per-table scan continuation, so repeated bounded calls
+cannot restart forever at the same restricted or read-through-retained roots;
+after reaching the end they wrap for roots whose blockers were removed.
+Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
+child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
+on its parent. Any error after an earlier cascade or set-null write rolls back
+the whole retirement transaction. A restricted root alone is an expected
+deferred cleanup, not an error for the sweep as a whole.

   148	        if target_ids.is_empty() { continue; }
   149	        let parent_t = tx.num(target)?;
   150	        for (old, next) in target_ids {

   159	    tx: &Tx<'_>,

   258	/-- Retire a due row that physically holds an inserted id. The native engine
   259	does this before checking the new image's remaining unique keys, in the same
   260	transaction as the insert. -/
   261	def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)
   262	    (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) : Except Stop Store :=
   263	  match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
   264	  | some old =>
   265	    if expired td now old then refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old
   266	    else pure s
   267	  | none => pure s
   268	
   269	/-- Whether `insert if absent` has a live unique-key occupant. Native checks
   270	all live unique collisions before retiring an expired same-id predecessor, so
   271	a no-op leaves the physical store and its action children unchanged. -/
   272	def insertIfAbsentClash (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   273	    (t : String) (td : TableDecl) (img : Row) : Except Stop Bool :=
   274	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   275	  | some (_, r) => do
   276	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) eRule
   277	    pure true
   278	  | none => pure false
   279	
   280	/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
   281	`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
   282	retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
   283	evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
   284	the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
   285	abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
   286	
   287	def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
   288	  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
   289	
   290	def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
   291	  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
   292	  | some (_, rs) => rs
   293	  | none => fallback t
   294	
   295	/-- Runtime's stable ancestor order is lexical when read-through is absent,
   296	as it is in this model fragment. Expiry retirement visits that order in
   297	reverse so peers cannot depend on declaration or mutation order. -/
   298	def expiryRetirementTables (sch : Schema) : List TableDecl :=
   299	  sch.tables.mergeSort fun a b => String.compare a.name b.name != .lt
   300	
   301	/-- In-engine continuation of the bounded expiry index walk. `table` rotates
   302	the next call after the last table that consumed a visit; `rows` carries the
   303	last `(selected index components,id)` key for a table whose page exhausted
   304	the call's limit. -/
   305	structure SweepCursor where
   306	  table : Option String := none
   307	  rows : List (String × Key) := []
   308	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq
   309	
   310	def SweepCursor.after (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) : Option Key :=
   311	  cursor.rows.lookup table
   312	
   313	def SweepCursor.mark (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) (key : Key) : SweepCursor :=
   314	  { table := some table, rows := (table, key) :: cursor.rows.filter fun p => p.1 != table }
   315	
   316	def SweepCursor.clear (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) : SweepCursor :=
   317	  { cursor with rows := cursor.rows.filter fun p => p.1 != table }
   318	
   319	def SweepCursor.toValue (cursor : SweepCursor) : Value :=
   320	  .row [("table", cursor.table.map (fun t => Value.s (.text (cps t))) |>.getD .null),
   321	    ("rows", .arr (cursor.rows.mergeSort (fun a b => String.compare a.1 b.1 != .gt) |>.map fun p =>
   322	      .row [("table", .s (.text (cps p.1))), ("key", .arr (p.2.map Value.s))]))]
   323	
   324	/-- Rotate a stable table order after a persisted table name. A stale name
   325	from an adopted schema leaves the new order unchanged. -/
   326	def rotateExpiryTables (tables : List TableDecl) : Option String → List TableDecl
   327	  | none => tables
   328	  | some after =>
   329	    let rec go (before : List TableDecl) : List TableDecl → List TableDecl
   330	      | [] => tables
   331	      | td :: rest => if td.name == after then rest ++ before.reverse ++ [td]
   332	        else go (td :: before) rest
   333	    go [] tables
   334	
   335	def expiryOrder (td : TableDecl) : List String :=
   336	  if td.expiryOrder.isEmpty then td.expire.toList else td.expiryOrder
   337	
   338	def dueRowsAfter (td : TableDecl) (physical : List Row) (now : Int)
   339	    (after : Option Key) : List Row :=
   340	  match td.expire with
   341	  | none => []
   342	  | some _ =>
   343	    let order := expiryOrder td
   344	    let due := (sortRows order false physical).filter (expired td now)

   346	    | none => due
   347	    | some key => due.filter fun row => keyCmp (rowKey order row) key == .gt
   348	
   349	structure SweepState where
   350	  rows : MaterialStore
   351	  cursor : SweepCursor
   352	  visited : Nat := 0
   353	
   354	/-- One native expiry-index walk. Native fetches at most 256 keys at a time;
   355	actions in that page can move or remove rows before the next scan. -/
   356	partial def sweepExpiryTable (sch : Schema) (base : Store) (now : Int) (limit : Nat)
   357	    (td : TableDecl) (wrapped : Bool) (state : SweepState) : SweepState :=
   358	  if state.visited >= limit then state else
   359	  let physical := state.rows.store base
   360	  let batch := min (limit - state.visited) 256
   361	  let candidates := (dueRowsAfter td (physical td.name) now (state.cursor.after td.name)).take batch
   362	  let count := candidates.length
   363	  let state := candidates.foldl (fun (state : SweepState) r =>
   364	    let key := rowKey (expiryOrder td) r
   365	    let cursor := state.cursor.mark td.name key
   366	    let physical := state.rows.store base

   375	    let state := { state with cursor := state.cursor.clear td.name }

   378	  else sweepExpiryTable sch base now limit td wrapped state
   379	
   380	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
   381	/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
   382	stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
   383	model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
   384	root can be retired immediately. The cursor persists across server sweep calls,

   386	def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (cursor : SweepCursor := {})

   394	    ) ({ rows := materialRows tables s, cursor } : SweepState)
   395	  (state.rows.store s, state.cursor)
   396	
   397	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — same-id replacement authorizes, retires with actions, then inserts.
   398	/-- Apply one write to the store. -/
   399	def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
   400	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>
   401	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   402	    | none => throw eInput
   403	    | some td => do
   404	      let fs ← scalarsE fields

   408	      -- predecessor is still present, then retires it and applies its actions.

   415	          doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   416	      else
   417	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   418	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   419	  | .update t key patch cond =>
   420	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   421	    | none => throw eInput
   422	    | some td => do
   423	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   424	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   425	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   426	      | none => throw notFound
   427	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
   428	  | .upsert t key patch =>
   429	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   430	    | none => throw eInput
   431	    | some td => do
   432	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   433	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   434	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   435	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
   436	      | none => do
   437	        let rid ← upsertId ks ps
   438	        let img ← buildImage td rid (ks ++ ps) notFound
   439	        guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) notFound
   440	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   441	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img notFound
   442	  | .delete t key =>

+#[test]
+fn seeded_source_retirement_precedes_final_exists_and_rolls_back() {
+    let source = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+table members:
+  conversationId: conversations
+  seen: int
+  cap 10 by conversationId
+  public
+table messages:
+  conversationId: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+table witnesses:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  unique byMessage: message
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table gates:
+  message: messages
+  public
+  after insert <- exists witnesses[message = .message] by byMessage
+table fixtures:
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversationId = m.conversationId and .ordinal > m.seen
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("seed-final-exists.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let schema: Schema = crate::json_codec::from_text(
+        &crate::json_codec::to_text(&bound.schema).unwrap(),
+    ).unwrap();
+    let message = |until| object([
+        ("id", id("m")), ("conversationId", id("c")),
+        ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("until", Value::Int(until)),
+    ]);
+    let witness = object([("id", id("w")), ("message", id("m"))]);
+    let gate = object([("id", id("g")), ("message", id("m"))]);
+
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(schema.clone(), vec![]).unwrap();
+    let refused = e.seed_at([
+        ("messages".into(), message(5)),
+        ("witnesses".into(), witness.clone()),
+        ("gates".into(), gate.clone()),
+    ], 10);
+    assert!(matches!(refused, Err(crate::RuntimeError::Constraint(_))), "{refused:?}");
+    for table in ["messages", "witnesses", "gates", "unread"] {
+        assert!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().is_empty(), "{table} survived refused seed");
+    }
+
+    // A live source leaves the witness intact, while an unrelated expired
+    // fixture retains the ordinary physical seed contract.
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(schema, vec![]).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("messages".into(), message(50)),
+        ("witnesses".into(), witness),
+        ("gates".into(), gate),
+        ("fixtures".into(), object([("id", id("f")), ("until", Value::Int(5))])),
+    ], 10).unwrap();
+    for table in ["messages", "witnesses", "gates", "fixtures"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}

 #[test]
+fn legacy_identity_adoption_can_change_the_grouping_key() {
+    let mut e = groups();
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    for old in rows {
+        tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+        let mut legacy = old.clone();
+        let id = crate::value::canonical_json(&[old.field("n").unwrap().clone()]);
+        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy {
+            fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(id));
+        }
+        tx.put("totals", &target, &legacy, None).unwrap();
+    }
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute(
+        "DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+        [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+    ).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(&GROUPS.replace("by .n", "by .bucket"));
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 10).unwrap();
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("id").unwrap(),
+        &Value::Id(crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(0)])));
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("bucket").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(4));
+}

+/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.

+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);

fn refuse_maintained_columns(schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some()) {return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_VIEW_KEY",message:"Postgres evaluation has no background recount runner; use the SQLite engine for row-keyed views (guide maintains)".into()});}
    if schema.tables.iter().all(|(name,table)| table.maintained.keys().all(|field|
        schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| &o.table == name && &o.column == field)
            && schema.table(&m.source).is_some_and(|s| !s.is_expiring() && s.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| &t.parent == name && m.by == [t.reference.clone()])))))
        && schema.maintains.iter().filter_map(|m|m.private.as_ref()).all(|o| schema.table(&o.table).is_some_and(|t|t.maintained.contains_key(&o.column))) { return Ok(()); }
    if schema.tables.values().any(|table| !table.maintained.is_empty())
        || schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.private.is_some())
    {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_POSTGRES_MAINTAINED_COLUMN",
            message: "Postgres evaluation does not support maintained columns or their private maintains; use the SQLite engine for maintained columns (guide maintains)".into() });
    }
    Ok(())
}

     1	import Quarry.Store
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Maintained aggregate identity
     5	
     6	The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
     7	tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
     8	cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
     9	store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
    10	lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
    11	and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
    12	identity while publishing the new version.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	namespace Quarry
    16	
    17	/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
    18	migration. -/
    19	def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
    20	
    21	/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
    22	not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
    23	to this logical model. -/

codex
I found a possible migration gap in the PostgreSQL adapter: its identity upgrade selects public aggregate targets, while the adapter also admits a narrow maintained-column form backed by private aggregate state. I’m tracing that form’s reads and writes to determine whether reopening can leave it using legacy ids.

+                target: Key::Key,

+    assert!(found.is_empty(), "{found:?}");

+        assert_eq!(write.named.get(UNHELD_UNIQUE), Some(&1), "{report:#?}");

+#[test]
+fn same_id_replacement_rechecks_an_unchanged_secondary_unique_key() {
+    let source = r#"
+table records:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  name: text <=20
+  unique name
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+mutation add(id: id, name: text <=20, expiresAt: time ?):
+  insert records { id, name, expiresAt }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([row("records", &[
+        ("id", id("p")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Int(900)),
+    ])], 500).unwrap();
+
+    let live = e.mutate("add", None, ctx("alice", &[
+        ("id", id("q")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
+    ])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&live), None, "an expired image releases its key: {live:?}");
+
+    let replace = e.mutate("add", None, ctx("alice", &[
+        ("id", id("p")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
+    ])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&replace).as_deref(), Some("E_UNIQUE"), "the replacement must see q's live key: {replace:?}");
+    let rows = e.store().rows("records").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 2, "the retirement rolls back with the refused replacement");
+    assert!(rows.iter().any(|r| r.field("id").is_ok_and(|v| *v == id("p"))
+        && r.field("expiresAt").is_ok_and(|v| *v == Value::Int(900))), "{rows:?}");
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_end_expiry_precedes_final_exists_checks() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by root
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+table markers:
+  child: children on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by child
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+  after insert <- exists children[.child]
+mutation create(expiresAt: time):
+  insert roots { id: 'r', expiresAt }
+  insert children { id: 'c', root: 'r' }
+  insert markers { id: 'm', child: 'c' }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    let out = e.mutate("create", None, ctx("alice", &[("expiresAt", Value::Int(900))])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&out).as_deref(), Some("E_CONSTRAINT"), "the cascade removes the final witness: {out:?}");
+    assert_eq!((count(&e, "roots"), count(&e, "children"), count(&e, "markers")), (0, 0, 0),
+        "the failed postcondition rolls back the whole mutation");
+}
+
+#[test]

+    let source = r#"
+table aRoots:

+  read <- allow
+  update <- allow

+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  read <- allow
+  update <- allow
+table children:
+  a: aRoots on delete cascade
+  z: zRoots
+  cap 2 by a
+  read <- allow
+mutation expireBoth():
+  update aRoots['a'] { expiresAt: 900 }
+  update zRoots['z'] { expiresAt: 900 }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        row("aRoots", &[("id", id("a")), ("expiresAt", Value::Null)]),
+        row("zRoots", &[("id", id("z")), ("expiresAt", Value::Null)]),
+        row("children", &[("id", id("c")), ("a", id("a")), ("z", id("z"))]),
+    ], 500).unwrap();
+    let out = e.mutate("expireBoth", None, ctx("alice", &[])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&out).as_deref(), Some("E_REFERENCED"), "zRoots retires before aRoots can cascade the blocker: {out:?}");
+    assert_eq!((count(&e, "aRoots"), count(&e, "zRoots"), count(&e, "children")), (1, 1, 1),
+        "the restrict refusal rolls back both expiry updates and every action");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("aRoots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").is_ok_and(|v| *v == Value::Null));
+    assert!(e.store().rows("zRoots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").is_ok_and(|v| *v == Value::Null));
+}

+/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
+`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
+retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
+evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
+the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
+abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
+
+def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
+  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
+
+def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
+  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
+  | some (_, rs) => rs
+  | none => fallback t
+
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
 /-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
 stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
 model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
 root can be retired immediately. -/
 def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
-  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
-    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
-      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
-      | .ok next => next
-      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
-      | .error _ => s
-    else s) s) s
+  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
+  let rows := sch.tables.foldl (fun rows td =>
+    let physical := rows.store s
+    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
+      let physical := rows.store s
+      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
+        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
+        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
+        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
+        | .error _ => rows
+      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
+  rows.store s

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..10002e01ee
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+//! Exact non-empty facts established by successful count guards.
+
+use super::*;
+use std::collections::BTreeSet;
+
+pub(super) const NONEMPTY: &str = "$aggregateNonempty";
+/// Capture marker for a local whose current value is an exact `count(domain)`
+/// observation. It lives on the result and every domain root: ordinary
+/// rebinding, a write, an authority edge, or a control-flow meet therefore
+/// destroys stale provenance without repurposing diagnostic `origins`.
+pub(super) const COUNT_CAPTURE: &str = "$aggregateCountCapture";
+
+impl Binder<'_> {
+    /// A non-empty observation survives evaluation of its guard only when the
+    /// complete condition is write-free. Unlike point facts, aggregate facts
+    /// deliberately admit filters and seeks because those are part of the
+    /// exact domain identity recorded below.
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_guard_safe(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
+        match value {
+            A::Name { .. } | A::Focal { .. } | A::Literal { .. } => true,
+            A::Array { items, .. } => items.iter().all(|item| self.aggregate_guard_safe(item)),
+            A::Object { fields, .. } => fields.iter().all(|field| field.value.as_ref().is_none_or(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))),
+            A::Unary { value, .. } | A::Assert { value, .. } | A::ShapeUse { base: value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+            A::Binary { left, right, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(left) && self.aggregate_guard_safe(right),
+            A::Member { base, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => self.catalog.functions.get(name).is_none_or(|function|
+                self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) == Some(&true))
+                && args.iter().all(|arg| self.aggregate_guard_safe(arg)),
+            A::Read(read) | A::Exists { read, .. } | A::Created { read, .. } => {
+                read.computed.values().all(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))
+                    && read.keys.iter().all(|key| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&key.value))
+                    && read.seeks.iter().all(|seek| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&seek.value))
+                    && read.filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|filter| self.aggregate_guard_safe(filter))
+                    && read.matching.as_deref().is_none_or(|matching| self.aggregate_guard_safe(matching))
+                    && read.range.as_ref().and_then(|range| range.cursor.as_deref()).is_none_or(|cursor| self.aggregate_guard_safe(cursor))
+            }
+            A::Shape { base, fields, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base)
+                && fields.iter().all(|field| match field {
+                    ShapeField::Field { value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+                    ShapeField::Spread { .. } | ShapeField::NamedSpread { .. } | ShapeField::Bare { .. } => true,
+                }),
+            A::If { then, condition, otherwise, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(then)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(condition)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(otherwise),
+            A::Merge(_) | A::Walk { .. } | A::Write { .. } => false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Record only implications that follow from count's nonnegative range.
+    /// The common authored form is `require n > 0`, where `n` was bound from
+    /// `count(domain)`; direct count calls use the same identity.
+    // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#4-non-empty-domain-proof — the fact belongs to the exact domain roots and transaction state.
+    pub(super) fn record_aggregate_nonempty(&mut self, condition: &A, truth: bool) {
+        if !truth { return; }
+        let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = condition else { return };
+        let (candidate, threshold, op) = if let Some(n) = literal_int(right) {
+            (left.as_ref(), n, op.as_str())
+        } else if let Some(n) = literal_int(left) {
+            let reversed = match op.as_str() { "<" => ">", "<=" => ">=", ">" => "<", ">=" => "<=", other => other };
+            (right.as_ref(), n, reversed)
+        } else { return };
+        let proves_positive = match op {
+            ">" => threshold >= 0,
+            ">=" | "=" => threshold >= 1,
+            "!=" => threshold == 0,
+            _ => false,
+        };
+        if !proves_positive { return; }
+        let Some((key, roots)) = self.count_key(candidate) else { return };
+        for root in roots {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&root).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(key.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(root, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_nonempty(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> bool {
+        self.aggregate_key(read).is_some_and(|(key, roots)| roots.iter().all(|root|
+            self.binding(root).is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&key) == Some(&Ty::Bool))))
+    }
+
+    /// Resolve count provenance before rebinding `name`: a count domain may
+    /// itself refer to the old value of that local. Such a self-dependent
+    /// capture cannot be represented by the post-assignment binding and is
+    /// therefore deliberately not narrowed.
+    pub(super) fn count_capture(&self, name: &str, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let A::Call { name: call, args, .. } = value else { return None };
+        if call != "count" || args.len() != 1 || self.catalog.functions.contains_key(call)
+            || !self.aggregate_guard_safe(value) { return None; }
+        let read = args.first().and_then(|arg| self.aggregate_domain(arg))?;
+        let (aggregate, roots) = self.aggregate_key(&read)?;
+        if roots.contains(name) { return None; }
+        let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), aggregate[1].clone()];
+        Some((capture, roots))
+    }
+
+    /// Attach pre-resolved capture-time provenance after assigning `name`.
+    /// `origins` remains diagnostic history; this field fact is the reaching
+    /// definition proof used by a later `require name > 0`.
+    pub(super) fn record_count_capture(&mut self, name: &str, capture: Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)>) {
+        let Some((capture, mut owners)) = capture else { return };
+        owners.insert(name.to_owned());
+        for owner in owners {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&owner).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(capture.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(owner, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn count_key(&self, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let (count_arg, captured_name) = match value {
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+            A::Name { name, .. } => self.binding(name)?.origins.iter().rev().find_map(|(_, origin)| match origin {
+                A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                    && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+                _ => None,
+            }),
+            _ => None,
+        }.map(|arg| (arg, match value { A::Name { name, .. } => Some(name.as_str()), _ => None }))?;
+        let result = self.aggregate_key(&self.aggregate_domain(count_arg)?)?;
+        if let Some(name) = captured_name {
+            let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), result.0[1].clone()];
+            if self.binding(name)?.fields.get(&capture) != Some(&Ty::Bool)
+                || !result.1.iter().all(|root| self.binding(root)
+                    .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&capture) == Some(&Ty::Bool)))
+            {
+                return None;
+            }
+        }
+        Some(result)
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_key(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        if read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() { return None; }
+        let mut roots = BTreeSet::new();
+        let keys = read.keys.iter().map(|key| Some(format!("{:?}:{}", key.column,
+            self.aggregate_value(&key.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let seeks = read.seeks.iter().map(|seek| Some(format!("{}:{}:{}", seek.column, seek.op,
+            self.aggregate_value(&seek.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let filter = match read.filter.as_deref() {
+            Some(value) => Some(self.aggregate_value(value, &mut roots)?),
+            None => None,
+        };
+        if roots.is_empty() { roots.insert(pure_calls::CONSTANTS.into()); }
+        let identity = format!("{:?}:{:?}:{:?}:{keys:?}:{seeks:?}:{filter:?}", read.table, read.index, read.order_keys);
+        Some((vec![NONEMPTY.into(), identity], roots))
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_value(&self, value: &A, roots: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
+        match value {
+            A::Focal { .. } => Some("focal".into()),
+            A::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Focal { .. }) => Some(format!("focal.{name}")),
+            A::Literal { .. } | A::Name { .. } | A::Member { .. } => self.stable_value(value, roots).map(|value| value.key()),
+            A::Unary { op, value, .. } => Some(format!("unary:{op}:{}", self.aggregate_value(value, roots)?)),
+            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => Some(format!("binary:{op}:{}:{}", self.aggregate_value(left, roots)?, self.aggregate_value(right, roots)?)),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
+                let function = self.catalog.functions.get(name)?;
+                if self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) != Some(&true) { return None; }
+                Some(format!("call:{name}:{:?}", args.iter().map(|arg| self.aggregate_value(arg, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?))
+            }
+            A::Array { items, .. } => Some(format!("array:{:?}", items.iter().map(|item| self.aggregate_value(item, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?)),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}

     /// After `require x != null` or inside `if x != null:`, `x` is present.
     pub(super) fn narrow(&mut self, condition: &A, then_branch: bool) {
+        // Aggregate facts may describe filtered domains, so they have a
+        // slightly wider write-free admission check than point facts. Record

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3708ad4a5a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";
+
+/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
+/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
+/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
+pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
+    mut tables: Vec<String>,
+    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
+) -> Vec<String> {
+    let after = cursors
+        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
+        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
+        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
+    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
+        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
+        tables.rotate_left(next);
+    }
+    tables
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
+    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
+}

    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)

    74	      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store

   105	def bindArgs (params : List Param) (args : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop Env :=
   106	  params.mapM fun p => match args.lookup p.name with
   107	    | some v => pure (p.name, (v, none))
   108	    | none => if p.optional then pure (p.name, (.null, none)) else throw (.refuse "E_INPUT")

   111	
   112	structure Case where
   113	  schema : Schema
   114	  helpers : List Helper := []
   115	  store : Store
   116	  viewer : List Nat
   117	  now : Int := 0
   118	  program : Program
   119	  args : List (String × Value) := []
   120	  budget : Option Nat := none

   122	  sweepOnly : Bool := false
   123	  /-- In-engine sweep continuation supplied by the differential driver. -/
   124	  sweepCursor : SweepCursor := {}
   125	  /-- Visited-row bound for the sweep; examples default to a complete pass. -/
   126	  sweepLimit : Option Nat := none

   128	def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
   129	  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
   130	    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }
   131	
   132	def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
   133	  | .normal => (.null, .null)
   134	  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)
   135	
   136	def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   137	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   138	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   139	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   140	  | .ok env =>
   141	    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now
   142	    match (execStmts queryHooks defaultFuel c.ctx vw env c.program.body).run {} with

   144	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   145	    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   146	
   147	def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   148	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   149	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   150	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   151	  | .ok env =>
   152	    match (execStmts mutationHooks defaultFuel c.ctx { store := c.store } env c.program.body).run {} with
   153	    | .ok ((fl, w, _), _) => match retireExpiredChanged c.schema c.now w.store
   154	        (changedRetirementOrder c.schema w.changed) with
   155	      | .ok s' => .committed (flowValue fl).1 s'
   156	      | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   157	      | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   158	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   159	    | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   160	
   161	def run (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   162	  if c.sweepOnly then
   163	    let (store, cursor) := sweepExpired c.schema c.store c.now c.sweepCursor c.sweepLimit
   164	    .committed cursor.toValue store
   165	  else match c.program.kind with
   166	    | .query => runQuery c
   167	    | .mutation => runMutation c
   168	
   169	end Quarry

   131	
   132	### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
   133	
   134	Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
   135	64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
   136	`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
   137	The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
   138	identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
   139	adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
   140	address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
   141	
   142	The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
   143	order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
   144	lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
   145	whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
   146	`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
   147	
   148	The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
   149	`maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
   150	function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
   151	0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON of the group key —
   152	atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate target from its source
   153	rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
   154	rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
   155	advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
   156	the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
   157	writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
   158	legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
   159	then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps, including
   160	rows, columns and narrowed rows retained in release-dormant storage. Its
   161	captured dormant-reference ledger changes in the same transaction, so a later
   162	restore still proves the same aggregate lifetime under its digest address. Thus an
   163	aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
   164	aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
   165	to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
   166	target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
   167	Removing the aggregate itself retires its derived target rows; a dormant
   168	reference to that retired target receives no map and keeps the ordinary
   169	restore refusal against acquiring a newly created parent lifetime.
   170	Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
   171	the same transaction. A legacy target address is itself the predecessor's
   172	canonical logical group tuple. Adoption decodes it using the predecessor
   173	maintain and column types, so candidate projection cannot erase the migration
   174	input when the same activation also changes the grouping declaration. The map
   175	preserves the predecessor target identity; the candidate rebuild then decides
   176	which new groups exist, so a reference to a removed group follows the ordinary
   177	dangling-reference contract. The fixed-point bound counts stored aggregate identities,
   178	not aggregate declarations, because one target can hold a legal acyclic chain
   179	of references to other rows in that same target. SQLite captures newly recorded
   180	path values while predecessor targets still exist, then derives and applies all
   181	legacy maps before any recorded-path rebuild can remove those targets. Schemas
   182	with ordinary maintains require device capability
   183	`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
   184	it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
   185	zero. Conversely, a current device refuses to execute backend bytes from an
   186	old server that omit this capability. The shared codec records the omission so
   187	the server can adopt and republish a persisted schema; a device may decode the
   188	same bytes only as an inactive kept predecessor that it atomically replaces
   189	with a current backend, preserving queued writes. Offline reuse and adoption
   190	of the old backend refuse before interpretation.

+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
+/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
+is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
+sweep. -/
+abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
+
+structure MutationWorld where
+  store : Store
+  changed : ChangedRows := []
+
+def RWrite.explicitId? : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
+  | .insert t fields _ => match fields.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => none
+  | .upsert t key patch =>
+    match key.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
+      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+      | _ => none
+  | _ => none
+
+def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
+  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
+    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
+    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
+    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
+
+def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
+  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
+  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
+    | .error e => .error e
+    | .ok (value, store) =>
+      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
+      let changed := match rw.explicitId? with | some address => changed ++ [address] | none => changed
+      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })
+
+/-- Retire only rows written by this mutation whose final image is already
+expired. A restrict refusal aborts the mutation; cascade and set-null actions
+are in the same transition. -/
+def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
+  | s, [] => pure s
+  | s, (t, rid) :: rest =>
+    match sch.table? t with
+    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+    | some td =>
+      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
+      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+      | some row =>
+        if expired td now row then do
+          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
+          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+

+    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
+    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
+    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
+    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
+    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
+    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
+        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
+            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
+            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
+                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
+                (field, kind)
+            }).collect();
+            let mut rows = Vec::new();
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (row, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
+                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
+                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
+                    rows.push((old, key));
+                }
+            }
+            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
+        }
+
+        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+        let mut settled = false;
+        for _ in 0..=legacy.len() {
+            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
+                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+                for (old, key) in rows {
+                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                        let mut value = value.clone();
+                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                        value
+                    }).collect();
+                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+                }
+            }
+            if next_ids == ids {
+                ids = next_ids;
+                settled = true;
+                break;
+            }
+            ids = next_ids;
+        }
+        if !settled {
+            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
+        }
+
+        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
+            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
+                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
+                .collect();
+            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
+        }).collect();
+        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+        for (name, table, columns) in references {
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (old, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let mut next = old.clone();
+                    let mut changed = false;
+                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
+                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
+                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    if changed {
+                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
+                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

16-the hand-kept `posts.score` with `update <- allow` that three consecutive Clique builders
17-wrote instead. This RFC proposes the same aggregate, by the same evaluator, **shown as a
18-column of the row it describes**:

34:**The mechanism (revision 3): a private maintain plus a mirror.** The declaration is a
35-`maintain` the author cannot see — the authoritative total for every parent id, live,
36-absent or expired, kept by today's maintain machinery unchanged — and an engine step that
37-copies the total onto the parent row whenever that row is present and live. Every hard
38-case the first two rounds found in keeping the total *only* on the row (what to do while
39-the parent is absent or expired, how to be born, how to die, where overflow is checked,
40:what a redefinition reconciles) has one answer: the private total is the truth, and the
41-column is its mirror.

97-  and tuples are the `maintain` form's.

99-  maintain's `sum` takes.

129:### 3.2 The mechanism: a private maintain, and its mirror
130-
131:**The private maintain.** The declaration generates a maintain — same kind, source,
132-predicate and `by` — whose target is an engine-named table the author cannot spell (its
133-name is not a Quarry identifier). It is a `Maintain` in `Schema.maintains` with a
134:`private` mark and the owning `(table, column)`; its target is **not** the parent table,
135-so `maintain_for(parent)` stays `None` and neither `classify`'s maintain-target bypass nor
136-`refuse_engine_owned` ever sees the application's table as engine-owned. It has no read
137-rule and is never synced — **and it does not inherit its source's `sync`**: today's binder
138-copies a source's audience onto any generated target whose `by` survives
139:(`bind/schema.rs`), which for public likes would put the private rows in the `public`
140-partition and make every device fail to apply an unknown table. The generated maintain is
141-outside `Schema.synced()` on the server as well as outside the projection. Everything else is today's maintain, unchanged:
142-`Runner::maintain`, `apply_aggregate`, the 53-bit check on **the one authoritative
143-value**, `rebuild_maintain`. It holds the total for every parent id that has one —
144-whether the parent is live, absent, expired or deleted.
145-
146-**"Private" is operational, not a naming convention.** An unspellable name and a denied
147-read rule stop neither a hand-serialized rule probing the target's `byGroup` (a probe does
148-not consult the probed table's read rule), nor a native job, which names tables as strings
149-and runs as the system. So:
150-
151:- *One predicate*, `visible`, decides every enumeration, and a private target and its
152-  `Maintain` fail it: both emitters (`api.ts` and the Rust module), `GET /` and **`GET
153-  /schema`**, `check`'s counts and listings, `check --residency`, `why`, `data` (including
154-  its suggestions), `sql`'s views, `/changes` — ordinary commit metadata **and** its
155-  saturated-page fallback, which today lists every schema table — and adoption
156:  diagnostics, which attribute the private table's steps to the owning column instead of
157-  reporting "a table is added". `doctor`'s table count uses `visible`, like `check`'s;
158-  its physical row and byte totals stay honest and say they include engine-internal
159-  storage.
160-- *A public schema projection.* `GET /schema` is the device's `Backend` today and sends the
161:  whole `Schema`. The device and every client receive a projection with **no private
162:  tables and no private maintains**; it carries, per maintained column, what a device
163-  needs — that the column is unwritable, that a missing value reads 0, and a **derivation
164-  identity** (a digest of kind, source, predicate and `by`). The identity is a **field of
165-  the projected table's column metadata** — part of the projected `Table` value that
166-  `successor::keeps_literal_default_images` compares — not a sidecar on the `/schema`
167:  envelope: the projection has no private maintains, so "the maintains differ" cannot be
168-  what tells a device that a redefined column's held images are stale. The server keeps
169-  the complete schema.
170-- *A core invariant.* No program, native call, rule, constraint, seed, fixture or
171:  hand-serialized IR or schema can address a private target — `Get`, `Scan`, an `exists`
172-  or `created` probe, or any write — **including under the system context**. Core
173-  validation refuses the schema or program; the runtime refuses the access; only the
174-  engine's own birth, mirror and rebuild path reaches the table. Every refusal and every
175:  diagnostic names the owning `(table, column)`, never the private name.
176-
177:**The mirror.** After **every** `apply_aggregate` return that changed the private total
178-for id X — a `put`, or the delete-to-zero that today returns without one — the engine
179-re-reads the parent's **current** image with **`tx.get` and `Table::expired`** (never
180-`fetch` or `get`, which consult rules and, on a device, record an unknown fact; and never
181-an image captured earlier in the commit, so two maintained columns changed in one commit
182-compose instead of clobbering each other). If P is present and live, it writes P's image
183-with the one field set to the new total — `tx.put(parent_table, table, new, Some(old))`,
184-`row_changed(.., Origin::Maintained)`. If P is absent or expired, it does nothing: an
