    40	        let probes = effects.iter().map(|effect| rule_probes(table.rules.for_effect(*effect))).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
    41	        if !self.meter.room(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes) {
    42	            return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::RuleProbes, actual: self.meter.used.rule_probes.saturating_add(probes), ceiling: self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes, site: self.meter.site().into() });
    43	        }
    44	        Ok(())
    45	    }
    46	
    47	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — reserve resolution's static worst case before the target lookup; no ceiling is changed.
    48	    pub(in crate::engine) fn reserve_target_resolution(&mut self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, patch: &crate::value::Supplied, upsert: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    49	        if upsert { self.reserve_capture(table)?; }
    50	        let probes = rule_probes(&table.rules.read).saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(rule_probes(&table.rules.update).saturating_mul(1 + u64::from(table.judges_old_image())))
    51	            .saturating_add(if upsert || table.ephemeral.is_some() { rule_probes(&table.rules.insert).saturating_mul(2) } else { 0 });
    52	        // Covers the largest cloned row allowed by the schema, the caller's patch
    53	        // (including ill-typed fields), and the miss arm's image/default materialization.
    54	        // Retained maps/assets share their Arc; the merge charges only memory it copies.
    55	        let witness = self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.read).max(self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.update))
    56	            .max(if upsert || table.ephemeral.is_some() { self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.insert) } else { 0 });
    57	        let copy = if crate::rows::disclosed::actual_size(table) { 0 } else { row_copy_ceiling(table).saturating_mul(2) };
    58	        let heap = copy.saturating_add(patch.heap_bytes().saturating_mul(2))
    59	            .max(crate::rows::disclosed::admission(table)).saturating_add(witness);
    60	        for (kind, amount, used, ceiling) in [(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes, self.meter.used.rule_probes, self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes),
    61	            (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap, self.meter.used.heap_bytes, self.meter.ceilings.heap_bytes),
    62	            (MeterKind::IndexEntries, if upsert { table.sequences.len() as u64 } else { 0 }, self.meter.used.index_entries, self.meter.ceilings.index_entries)] {
    63	            if !self.meter.room(kind, amount) { return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual: used.saturating_add(amount), ceiling, site: self.meter.site().into() }); }
    64	        }
    65	        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
    66	        Ok(())
    67	    }
    68	
    69	    /// The merged image and its lawful copy price (LLP 3000.015 §1), which a
    70	    /// later engine copy of the same image charges again.
    71	    pub(in crate::engine) fn merge_patch(&mut self, table: &str, old: &Value, patch: &crate::value::Supplied, _readable: bool) -> Result<(Value, u64), RuntimeError> {
    72	        let public = if crate::rows::disclosed::actual_size(&self.schema.tables[table]) {
    73	            self.authorize_image(table, old.clone())?
    74	        } else { None };
    75	        let mut bytes = 40_u64;
    76	        for (key, _) in old.as_object()?.iter().filter(|(key, _)| !patch.as_object().expect("patch checked").contains_key(*key)).chain(patch.as_object()?.iter()) {
    77	            // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — a retained field's actual size is disclosed
    78	            // only after both row and field read authority succeed.
    79	            let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
    80	            let copy = if patch.as_object()?.contains_key(key) { patch.field_copy(key) } else if let Some(row) = &public { row.scalar_heap(key) } else { definition.columns.get(key).map_or(0,column_copy_ceiling) };
    81	            bytes = bytes.saturating_add(80 + key.len() as u64 + copy);
    82	        }
    83	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
    84	        let fields = old.as_object()?.iter().filter(|(key, _)| !patch.as_object().expect("patch checked").contains_key(*key)).chain(patch.as_object()?.iter())
    85	            .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), value.clone())).collect::<std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _>>();
    86	        Ok((Value::Row(fields.into()), bytes))
    87	    }
    88	
    89	    pub(in crate::engine) fn no_write_target(&self) -> RuntimeError {
    90	        RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".into(), message: None }
    91	    }
    92	
    93	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — item 7: an unheld write target without an absence proof queues.
    94	    pub(in crate::engine) fn write_miss(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> RuntimeError {
    95	        if self.device {
    96	            self.unknown_fact(table, index, key, &self.statement_site.clone());
    97	            if let Some(message) = &mut self.missing_fact { *message = message.replace("the row or its absence is past the acquired horizon or online only", "the write target is not held on this device; only the server can resolve it"); }
    98	            RuntimeError::Prediction(self.missing_fact.clone().expect("missing site recorded"))
    99	        } else { self.no_write_target() }
   100	    }
   101	
   102	    pub(in crate::engine) fn upsert_absence_proven(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   103	        let expressions: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|value| {
   104	            if *value == Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone()) { Expr::Input(Input::Viewer) } else { Expr::Literal(value.clone()) }
   105	        }).collect();
   106	        let Ok(visibility) = crate::engine::rules::upsert_absence(self.schema, table, index, &expressions) else { return Ok(false) };
   107	        if self.retained_group(table, index, key)? { return Ok(false); }
   108	        if visibility.decided_true { return Ok(true); }
   109	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — the parent key decides authorization; the child's acquired partition separately proves absence.
   110	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
   111	        let rule = definition.rules.read.device_audience_rule().into_owned();
   112	        if let Some(through) = &definition.through
   113	            && !rule.is_uniformly_readable()
   114	            && let Some(id) = definition.index(index).expect("checked index").columns().iter().zip(key).find_map(|(column, value)| (column == &through.reference).then_some(value))
   115	        {
   116	            let verdict = self.device_work(|runner| runner.parent_verdict(table, through, id))?;
   117	            return Ok(verdict == crate::engine::through::ParentVerdict::Readable && !self.beyond_horizon);
   118	        }
   119	        // A uniform key can still name somebody else's private group. Evaluate
   120	        // the rule over only its pinned columns, never using trust_synced_read:
   121	        // the synthetic row was not delivered. A positive membership witness
   122	        // may establish readability; an unknown probe must still queue.
   123	        let row = crate::value::Supplied::key(definition.index(index).expect("checked index"),key,&TargetInput(()));
   124	        let viewer = self.context.viewer.clone();
   125	        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
   126	        let readable = self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(&rule), &[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, rule_probes(&rule))], |runner, allowance| {
   127	            crate::engine::rules::evaluate(&rule, &viewer, None, &row, false, &mut crate::engine::read::RuleProbe { runner, allowance })
   128	        })?;
   129	        Ok(readable && !self.beyond_horizon)
   130	    }
   131	
   132	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — key absence is not insert authority: the materialized image and every colliding/counting population need the same held-group proof.
   133	    pub(in crate::engine) fn prove_upsert_insert(&mut self, table: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   134	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
   135	        let image_key = index_values(definition.index(addressed_index).expect("addressed index"), row);
   136	        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(table, addressed_index, &image_key)? {
   137	            return Err(self.write_miss(table, addressed_index, &image_key));
   138	        }
   139	        // byId is either the already-proven addressed key or a fresh minted id.
   140	        // Every application unique key can collide with a different, hidden row.
   141	        for (name, index) in definition.indexes.iter().filter(|(name, index)| index.unique && name.as_str() != "byId" && name.as_str() != addressed_index) {
   142	            let key = index_values(index, row);
   143	            if !key.contains(&Value::Null) && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table, name, &key)? {
   144	                return Err(self.write_miss(table, name, &key));
   145	            }
   146	        }
   147	        for constraint in &definition.constraints {
   148	            if let Constraint::Cap { by, .. } = constraint {
   149	                let key: Vec<_> = by.iter().map(|field| row.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect();
   150	                if self.schema.cap_skips_null(definition, by, &key) { continue; }
   151	                let Some((name, _)) = definition.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(by)) else {
   152	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("cap by {} has no leading index", by.join(", "))));
   153	                };
   154	                // An empty prefix is a whole-table cap: only full public sync
   155	                // covers it. A private viewer partition cannot count hidden rows.
   156	                if !self.upsert_absence_proven(table, name, &key)? { return Err(self.write_miss(table, name, &key)); }
   157	            }
   158	        }
   159	        Ok(())
   160	    }
   161	
   162	    pub(in crate::engine) fn write_target(&mut self, target: &Read, patch: &Expr, upsert: bool, condition: Option<&WriteCondition>, valued: bool) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
   163	        self.target_attempt(&target.table, |runner| runner.resolve_write_target(target, patch, upsert, condition, valued))
   164	    }
   165	
   166	    pub(in crate::engine) fn delete_target(&mut self, target: &Read) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   167	        self.target_attempt(&target.table, |runner| {
   168	            runner.refuse_engine_owned(&target.table, Effect::Delete)?;
   169	            let key = target.key.iter().map(|e| runner.expr(e)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
   170	            let table = runner.schema.table(&target.table).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {}", target.table)))?;
   171	            let index = table.index(&target.index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing index {}.{}", target.table, target.index)))?;
   172	            if !index.unique || key.len() != index.columns().len() { return Err(RuntimeError::Input("a write target needs one complete unique key".into())); }
   173	            runner.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
   174	            runner.reserve_maintains(&target.table, table)?;
   175	            runner.read_tables.insert(target.table.clone());
   176	            let old = runner.lookup_write_occupant(&target.table, &target.index, index, &key)?;
   177	            if runner.device && (table.sync.is_none() || (old.is_none() && !runner.upsert_absence_proven(&target.table, &target.index, &key)?)) {
   178	                return Err(runner.write_miss(&target.table, &target.index, &key));
   179	            }
   180	            let Some(old) = old else { return Err(runner.no_write_target()); };
   181	            // Preserve alternate delete's existing read gate, without exposing
   182	            // the private target or charging a hidden population through Get.
   183	            if runner.inactive_write_target(&target.table, &old)? || !runner.check_rule(&target.table, Effect::Read, None, &old)? { runner.refusing_clause(&target.table, "read rule"); return Err(runner.no_write_target()); }
   184	            if !runner.check_rule(&target.table, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
   185	                return Err(RuntimeError::Rule { table: target.table.clone(), effect: Effect::Delete });
   186	            }
   187	            runner.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   188	            runner.delete_authorized(&target.table, old)
   189	        })
   190	    }
   191	
   192	    fn resolve_write_target(&mut self, target: &Read, patch: &Expr, upsert: bool, condition: Option<&WriteCondition>, valued: bool) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
   193	        if upsert { self.refuse_upsert_owned(&target.table)?; }
   194	        else { self.refuse_engine_owned(&target.table, Effect::Update)?; }
   195	        if upsert && condition.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Input("a condition belongs on update; an upsert inserts or patches".into())); }
   196	        if let Some(condition) = condition { validate_condition(condition)?; }
   197	        let key = target.key.iter().map(|e| self.expr(e)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
   198	        let patch = self.expr_input(patch)?;
   199	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(&target.table, &patch, false)?;
   200	        self.refuse_recorded(&target.table, &patch)?;
   201	        crate::engine::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[&target.table], &target.table, &patch)?;
   202	        let definition = self.schema.table(&target.table).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {}", target.table)))?;
   203	        let index = definition.index(&target.index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing index {}.{}", target.table, target.index)))?;
   204	        if !index.unique || key.len() != index.columns().len() { return Err(RuntimeError::Input("a write target needs one complete unique key".into())); }
   205	        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") { return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{} update patch cannot change id", target.table))); }
   206	        self.read_tables.insert(target.table.clone());
   207	        self.reserve_target_resolution(&target.table, definition, &patch, upsert)?;
   208	        self.observe_sequence_selection(&target.table, &target.index, &key)?;
   209	        let old = self.lookup_write_occupant(&target.table, &target.index, index, &key)?;
   210	        if self.device && (definition.sync.is_none() || (old.is_none() && (!upsert || !self.upsert_absence_proven(&target.table, &target.index, &key)?))) {
     1	//! Parent authorization is shared; device acquisition remains a separate fact.
     2	// @ref LLP 3000.014#5 — only matching live current captures may borrow a parent verdict.
     3	use super::{rules::{self, Verdict}, runner::Runner, through::{ParentVerdict, capture_matches, stamp}};
     4	use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, rows::{Bounds, Dir}, schema::{Audience, through::*}, value::Value};
     5	
     6	impl Runner<'_> {
     7	    // @ref LLP 3000.014#5.1 — never enumerate aggregate keys before the parent verdict.
     8	    pub(super) fn aggregate_parent_prefix(&mut self, scan: &crate::ir::Scan, prefix: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<bool>, RuntimeError> {
     9	        let Some(m) = self.schema.maintain_for(&scan.table).filter(|m| m.groups_by_parent(self.schema)) else { return Ok(None) };
    10	        let parent = m.parent_key.as_ref();
    11	        let id = parent.and_then(|p| self.schema.tables[&scan.table].indexes[&scan.index].columns().iter().position(|f| f == &p.reference)).and_then(|at| prefix.get(at));
    12	        let (Some(parent), Some(id)) = (parent, id) else {
    13	            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_READ_THROUGH_SCAN", message: format!("{} at {} needs one pinned readable parent; use the parent page with a nested keyed totals read (guide maintains)", scan.table, scan.site) });
    14	        };
    15	        self.read_tables.insert(scan.table.clone());
    16	        self.read_tables.insert(m.source.clone());
    17	        let verdict = self.parent_verdict(&m.source, parent, id)?;
    18	        let unknown = verdict == ParentVerdict::Unknown || self.device && (self.beyond_horizon || self.schema.tables[&scan.table].sync.is_none());
    19	        if unknown {
    20	            self.unknown_fact(&scan.table, &scan.index, prefix, &scan.site);
    21	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.speculative = true);
    22	        }
    23	        Ok(Some(!unknown && verdict == ParentVerdict::Readable))
    24	    }
    25	
    26	    pub(super) fn parent_verdict(&mut self, child: &str, through: &Through, id: &Value) -> Result<ParentVerdict, RuntimeError> {
    27	        let parent = &self.schema.tables[&through.parent];
    28	        self.read_tables.insert(through.parent.clone());
    29	        self.rule_dependencies(&parent.rules.read);
    30	        for (kind, amount) in [
    31	            (MeterKind::Examined, 1),
    32	            (MeterKind::RuleProbes, rules::rule_probes(&parent.rules.read)),
    33	            (MeterKind::HeapBytes, super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(parent)),
    34	        ] {
    35	            if !self.read_charge(kind, amount)? { return Ok(ParentVerdict::Unknown); }
    36	        }
    37	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — the parent fetch draws from the request's physical allowance; its logical charges were reserved above.
    38	        let parent_id = id.as_str()?.to_owned();
    39	        let row = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.get(scope, &through.parent, &parent_id))?;
    40	        let live = row.as_ref().filter(|row| !self.expired(parent, row));
    41	        if self.device {
    42	            self.read_tables.insert(child.into());
    43	            if !self.read_charge(MeterKind::HeapBytes, super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[child]).saturating_mul(2))? { return Ok(ParentVerdict::Unknown); }
    44	            if !self.captures_match(child, through, id, live)? { return Ok(ParentVerdict::Unknown); }
    45	        }
    46	        let Some(row) = live else {
    47	            let covered = !self.device || match &row {
    48	                Some(row) => self.tx.current_row(&through.parent, row)?,
    49	                None => self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.authorization_absence_covered(scope, &through.parent, "byId", &[id.clone()]))?
    50	                    && self.tx.current_group(&through.parent, "byId", &[id.clone()])?,
    51	            };
    52	            return Ok(if covered { ParentVerdict::Absent } else { ParentVerdict::Unknown });
    53	        };
    54	        if self.device && !(self.is_provisional(&through.parent, row)? || self.tx.current_row(&through.parent, row)?) {
    55	            return Ok(ParentVerdict::Unknown);
    56	        }
    57	        let verdict = if self.context.is_system() { Verdict::Readable } else { self.read_authority(&through.parent, row, true)? };
    58	        match verdict {
    59	            Verdict::Unknown => Ok(ParentVerdict::Unknown),
    60	            Verdict::Denied => Ok(ParentVerdict::Unreadable),
    61	            Verdict::Readable => {
    62	                self.note_expiry(parent, row);
    63	                // A parent authorizes; it cannot certify acquisition of its children.
    64	                if self.device && !self.child_coverage(child, through, row)? {
    65	                    self.unknown_fact(child, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], "read through child coverage");
    66	                }
    67	                Ok(ParentVerdict::Readable)
    68	            }
    69	        }
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    pub(super) fn child_coverage(&self, child: &str, through: &Through, parent_row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    73	        let table = &self.schema.tables[child];
    74	        let Some(sync) = &table.sync else { return Ok(false) };
    75	        if sync.horizon.is_some() || self.is_provisional(&through.parent, parent_row)? { return Ok(false); }
    76	        let mut image = crate::value::object([(through.reference.clone(), parent_row.field("id")?.clone())]);
    77	        stamp(&self.schema.tables[&through.parent], through, parent_row, &mut image)?;
    78	        let columns = match &sync.audience {
    79	            Audience::Public => vec![],
    80	            Audience::Column(column) => vec![column.clone()],
    81	            Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.clone(),
    82	        };
    83	        let Some((index, _)) = table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(&columns)) else { return Ok(false) };
    84	        let prefix = columns.iter().map(|column| image.field(column).cloned()).collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
    85	        self.tx.current_group(child, index, &prefix)
    86	    }
    87	
    88	    pub(super) fn captured_aggregate_coverage(&mut self, maintain: &crate::schema::Maintain, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    89	        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
    90	        self.read_tables.insert(maintain.source.clone());
    91	        let Some(sync) = source.sync.as_ref().filter(|sync| sync.horizon.is_none()) else { return Ok(false) };
    92	        let fields: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = crate::small_map::collect(index.columns().into_iter().zip(key).map(|(field, value)| (maintain.aliases.get(&field).cloned().unwrap_or(field), value)));
    93	        let columns = match &sync.audience { Audience::Public => vec![], Audience::Column(column) => vec![column.clone()], Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.clone() };
    94	        let Some(prefix) = columns.iter().map(|column| fields.get(column).map(|value| (*value).clone())).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>() else { return Ok(false) };
    95	        let Some((index, _)) = source.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(&columns)) else { return Ok(false) };
    96	        self.tx.current_group(&maintain.source, index, &prefix)
    97	    }
    98	
    99	    fn captures_match(&mut self, child: &str, through: &Through, id: &Value, parent: Option<&Value>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let table = &self.schema.tables[child];
   101	        let mut expected = crate::value::object([] as [(&str, Value); 0]);
   102	        if let Some(parent) = parent { stamp(&self.schema.tables[&through.parent], through, parent, &mut expected)?; }
   103	        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   104	        loop {
   105	            let scratch = self.meter.mark();
   106	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| runner.tx.scan_metered(scope, child, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 1, &mut runner.meter))?;
   107	            if self.read_capped() { return Ok(false); }
   108	            let Some((row, key)) = page.into_iter().next() else { return Ok(true) };
   109	            if !self.read_charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)? || !self.read_charge(MeterKind::Steps, through.fields.len() as u64 + 1)? { return Ok(false); }
   110	            let current = !self.expired(table, &row) && !self.tx.retained_row(child, &row)?;
   111	            if current && (parent.is_none() || !capture_matches(through, &expected, &row)) { return Ok(false); }
   112	            bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key).map(|key| key.into_iter().skip(1).collect());
   113	            // One cursor is retained, with a schema-sized reservation; row scratch is reusable.
   114	            self.meter.release_heap(scratch);
   115	        }
   116	    }
   117	}
   345	    /// One engine write (delete or set-null update) of a `table` row: fetch and
   346	    /// write it, its index entries (a `words(..)` index at its token bound), a
   347	    /// row copy, and the source-write price the engine exports for the table.
   348	    fn unit_write(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   349	        let table = self.table(name)?;
   350	        let plan = self.write_reservation(name)?;
   351	        if plan.server_only { return None; }
   352	        let entries = table.indexes.values().map(|index| match index.word_component() {
   353	            Some((_, fields)) => fields.iter().filter_map(|f| table.columns.get(f)).map(|kind| match kind.required() {
   354	                ColumnType::Text { max } => u64::from(*max), _ => 0,
   355	            }).sum::<u64>().min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64),
   356	            None => 1,
   357	        }).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   358	        let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(table);
   359	        // The row copy and every phase's heap are held together until the
   360	        // write's attempt ends (an asset phase beside a column recount): a sum.
   361	        let mut unit = [4 + 2 * entries, 2 * entries, 1, 1, row.saturating_mul(4), 0, 0];
   362	        for phase in 0..=reservations::VIEW_READ {
   363	            add(&mut unit, plan.price(phase));
   364	        }
   365	        // The lifetime hook reserves all child-table witnesses while source

   236	    /// meter; they do no authorization traversal. A nested scope cannot opt
   237	    /// out of its enclosing authorization's physical allowance.
   238	    pub(super) fn prepaid_scan<T: Default>(&mut self, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], physical: bool, scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   239	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   240	        // This meter is the device's separate physical-work budget. Its
   241	        // caller maps exhaustion to uncertainty, never a logical E_BOUND.
   242	        if self.device_work_active {
   243	            let active = self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || (physical && !self.context.is_system()));
   244	            let result = scan(self, &Authorization::internal());
   245	            self.tx.authorizing.set(active);
   246	            return result;
   247	        }
   248	        for &(kind, amount) in allowance {
   249	            if !self.read_charge(kind, amount)? { return Ok(T::default()); }
   250	        }
   251	        if self.read_capped() { return Ok(T::default()); }
   252	        let scope = Authorization { probes: Cell::new(0), remaining_probes: self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes.saturating_sub(self.meter.used.rule_probes) };

   254	        let result = scan(self, &scope);
   255	        self.leave_prepaid(state, result.as_ref().err());

   268	            ceilings: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.ceilings, Ceilings::unbounded()),
   269	            cut: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.cut, Cut::Abort),

+/// schema-semantic difference: server adoption compares and republishes the
+/// same schema after upgrading its stored representation.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
+pub struct LegacySemanticCapabilities(BTreeSet<String>);
+impl std::ops::Deref for LegacySemanticCapabilities {
+    type Target = BTreeSet<String>;
+    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target { &self.0 }

   188	
   189	/// Why [`lean`] produced no module.
   190	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   191	pub enum LeanError {
   192	    /// The sources do not compile; the model takes only checked programs.
   193	    Diagnostics(Vec<String>),
   194	    /// A schema-level construct outside the fragment.
   195	    Unsupported(Unsupported),
   196	}
   197	
   198	/// Check `sources` with [`crate::compile`], then translate their surface
   199	/// trees. A program outside the fragment is recorded per program in
   200	/// [`LeanModule::programs`]; a schema construct outside it refuses the whole
   201	/// module.
   202	pub fn lean(sources: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<LeanModule, LeanError> {
   203	    let bound = crate::compile(sources);
   204	    if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
   205	        return Err(LeanError::Diagnostics(bound.diagnostics.iter().map(|d| format!("{}: {}", d.code, d.message)).collect()));
   206	    }
   207	    let documents: Vec<Document> = sources.iter().map(|(file, source)| crate::parse_document(file, source).0).collect();
   208	    let expiry_orders = bound.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   209	        let column = table.expire.as_deref()?;
   210	        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain()
   211	            && index.columns().first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column))
   212	            .map(|(_, index)| (name.clone(), index.columns()))
   213	    }).collect();
   214	    from_documents_with_expiry(&documents, &expiry_orders).map_err(LeanError::Unsupported)
   215	}

   337	/// Compare one case whose source compiles. `Err` is a harness or emitter
   338	/// defect (never a verdict).
   339	pub fn compare(case: &Case, source: &str) -> Result<Checked, String> {
   340	    let unsupported = |reason: String| Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Unsupported(reason), executed: 0, pages: 0, mutation: false, class: String::new() });
   341	    let module = match module(source) {
   342	        Ok(m) => m,
   343	        Err(reason) => return unsupported(reason),
   344	    };
   345	    let mutation = case.program.mutation();
   346	    if let Err(u) = module.program("run") {
   347	        return unsupported(u.reason);
   348	    }
   349	    if mutation {
   350	        if let Err(u) = module.program("observe") {
   351	            return unsupported(format!("observe-{}", u.reason));
   352	        }
   353	    }

   355	        Ok(s) => s,
   356	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   357	    };
   358	    let mut m_args = match module.tag_args("run", &case.args) {
   359	        Ok(a) => a,
   360	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),

   362	    // The prelude: each step on the engine and on the model's store, in order.
   363	    for i in 0..case.steps.len() {
   364	        if let Err(u) = module.program(&format!("prep{i}")) {
   365	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   366	        }
   367	        if let Err(u) = module.tag_args(&format!("prep{i}"), &case.steps[i].args) {
   368	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   369	        }
   370	    }
   371	    let (mut engine, prelude) = execute::world(case, source)?;
   372	    engine.set_ceilings(Ceilings::default());
   373	    let mut executed = 0;
   374	    let mut pages = 0;
   375	    let mut store = store;
   376	    let mut sweep_cursor: Option<Json> = None;
   377	    let mut steps = prelude.iter();
   378	    let mut trail = vec![];
   379	    for (i, step) in case.steps.iter().enumerate() {
   380	        let name = format!("prep{i}");
   381	        if step.sweep {
   382	            let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("prelude sweep outcome missing")?;
   383	            if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   384	                return Err(format!("engine prelude sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   385	            }
   386	            let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   387	            let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);

   394	            store = swept["store"].clone();

   401	        executed += 2;

   403	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));

   406	        }
   407	        if m.kind == "committed" {

+fn seeded_expired_row_view_sources_do_not_revive_on_clock_rollback() {
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(compile(false), vec![]).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("members".into(), member(0, 0, 0))], 1).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("messages".into(), message(0, 1, 99, false, Some(100)))], 1).unwrap();
+
+    // Updating a live source into an expired final image and seeding a new
+    // born-expired source both retire through the common action path.
+    e.seed_at([

+        ("messages".into(), message(1, 1, 99, false, Some(5))),
+    ], 10).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    // Ordinary expired fixture images keep the seed contract.
+    let grant = with_deadline(object([
+        ("id", id("expired-grant")),
+        ("conversationId", id("room")),
+        ("principal", id("reader")),
+    ]), Some(5));
+    e.seed_at([("access".into(), grant)], 10).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("access").unwrap().len(), 1);
+
+    // A later rollback cannot resurrect either retired source into the live
+    // acquisition, even though both deadlines would otherwise be live at 2.
+    let views = e.store().rows("unread").unwrap();
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, Context::new("reader", Default::default()).at(2),
+        Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), 0);
+    let acquired = runner.live_acquisition_batch("unread", &views).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(acquired.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(acquired[0].as_ref().map(|row| field(row, "value")), Some(0));
+}

 def expiryRetirementTables (sch : Schema) : List TableDecl :=
   sch.tables.mergeSort fun a b => String.compare a.name b.name != .lt
 
+/-- In-engine continuation of the bounded expiry index walk. `table` rotates
+the next call after the last table that consumed a visit; `rows` carries the
+last `(selected index components,id)` key for a table whose page exhausted
+the call's limit. -/
+structure SweepCursor where
+  table : Option String := none
+  rows : List (String × Key) := []
+  deriving Repr, DecidableEq
+
+def SweepCursor.after (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) : Option Key :=
+  cursor.rows.lookup table
+
+def SweepCursor.mark (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) (key : Key) : SweepCursor :=
+  { table := some table, rows := (table, key) :: cursor.rows.filter fun p => p.1 != table }
+
+def SweepCursor.clear (cursor : SweepCursor) (table : String) : SweepCursor :=
+  { cursor with rows := cursor.rows.filter fun p => p.1 != table }
+
+def SweepCursor.toValue (cursor : SweepCursor) : Value :=
+  .row [("table", cursor.table.map (fun t => Value.s (.text (cps t))) |>.getD .null),
+    ("rows", .arr (cursor.rows.mergeSort (fun a b => String.compare a.1 b.1 != .gt) |>.map fun p =>
+      .row [("table", .s (.text (cps p.1))), ("key", .arr (p.2.map Value.s))]))]
+
+/-- Rotate a stable table order after a persisted table name. A stale name
+from an adopted schema leaves the new order unchanged. -/
+def rotateExpiryTables (tables : List TableDecl) : Option String → List TableDecl
+  | none => tables
+  | some after =>
+    let rec go (before : List TableDecl) : List TableDecl → List TableDecl
+      | [] => tables
+      | td :: rest => if td.name == after then rest ++ before.reverse ++ [td]
+        else go (td :: before) rest
+    go [] tables
+
+def expiryOrder (td : TableDecl) : List String :=
+  if td.expiryOrder.isEmpty then td.expire.toList else td.expiryOrder
+
+def dueRowsAfter (td : TableDecl) (physical : List Row) (now : Int)
+    (after : Option Key) : List Row :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => []
+  | some _ =>
+    let order := expiryOrder td
+    let due := (sortRows order false physical).filter (expired td now)
+    match after with
+    | none => due
+    | some key => due.filter fun row => keyCmp (rowKey order row) key == .gt
+
+structure SweepState where
+  rows : MaterialStore
+  cursor : SweepCursor
+  visited : Nat := 0
+
+/-- One native expiry-index walk. Native fetches at most 256 keys at a time;
+actions in that page can move or remove rows before the next scan. -/
+partial def sweepExpiryTable (sch : Schema) (base : Store) (now : Int) (limit : Nat)
+    (td : TableDecl) (wrapped : Bool) (state : SweepState) : SweepState :=
+  if state.visited >= limit then state else
+  let physical := state.rows.store base
+  let batch := min (limit - state.visited) 256
+  let candidates := (dueRowsAfter td (physical td.name) now (state.cursor.after td.name)).take batch
+  let count := candidates.length
+  let state := candidates.foldl (fun (state : SweepState) r =>
+    let key := rowKey (expiryOrder td) r
+    let cursor := state.cursor.mark td.name key
+    let physical := state.rows.store base
+    let rows := if stored physical td.name r then
+      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
+      | .ok next => materialRows (sch.tables.map (·.name)) next
+      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => state.rows
+      | .error _ => state.rows
+      else state.rows
+    { rows, cursor, visited := state.visited + 1 }) state
+  if count < batch then
+    let state := { state with cursor := state.cursor.clear td.name }
+    if !wrapped && state.visited < limit then sweepExpiryTable sch base now limit td true state
+    else state
+  else sweepExpiryTable sch base now limit td wrapped state
+

 /-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never

-  rows.store s
+  let limit := limit.getD (storeSize sch s + 1)
+  let ordered := rotateExpiryTables (expiryRetirementTables sch) cursor.table

 use super::*;
 use crate::schema::{ColumnDefault, ColumnType, materialize_optional_fields};
 use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
-use std::collections::BTreeSet;
+use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
 
 pub(crate) const VERSION: &str = "snapback4-release-store-3";
 
@@ -63,6 +63,98 @@ fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>)
     }
 }
 
+fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
+    kind: &ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+fn rewrite_legacy_row(
+    table: &Table,
+    row: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return false };
+    table.columns.iter().fold(false, |changed, (column, kind)| {
+        fields.get_mut(column).is_some_and(|value| rewrite_legacy_reference(kind, value, ids)) || changed
+    })
+}
+
+/// Rewrite references retained outside the active namespace alongside their
+/// active counterparts. References whose aggregate target was itself retired
+/// have no map and retain the ordinary dormant-lifetime refusal on restore.
+// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — identity adoption covers every surviving typed reference, including dormant storage.
+pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(
+    tx: &Tx<'_>,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    if ids.values().all(BTreeMap::is_empty) || !enabled(tx)? { return Ok(0); }
+    let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+
+    let cells = tx.conn().prepare(
+        "SELECT v.t,v.id,v.column_name,v.data,c.definition FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog k ON k.num=v.t JOIN _dormant_columns c ON c.table_name=k.name AND c.column_name=v.column_name ORDER BY v.t,v.id,v.column_name"
+    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?, row.get::<_,String>(4)?)))?
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
+    for (t, id, column, data, definition) in cells {
+        let definition: Column = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_reference(&definition.kind, &mut value, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_values SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3 AND column_name=?4", params![canonical_json(&value),t,id,column])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    let rows = tx.conn().prepare(
+        "SELECT r.t,r.id,r.data,d.definition FROM _dormant_rows r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t JOIN _dormant_tables d ON d.table_name=c.name ORDER BY r.t,r.id"
+    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
+    for (t, id, data, definition) in rows {
+        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
+        tx.conn().prepare(
+            "SELECT t,id,data,definition FROM _dormant_narrow_rows ORDER BY t,id"
+        )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
+            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?
+    } else { Vec::new() };
+    for (t, id, data, definition) in narrowed {
+        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_narrow_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    for (target, target_ids) in ids {
+        if target_ids.is_empty() { continue; }
+        let parent_t = tx.num(target)?;
+        for (old, next) in target_ids {
+            tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _dormant_refs(t,id,column_name,parent_t,parent_id,invalid) SELECT t,id,column_name,parent_t,?1,invalid FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3", params![next,parent_t,old])?;
+            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2", params![parent_t,old])?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(rewritten)
+}
+

     tx: &Tx<'_>,
     t: i64,

+#[test]
+fn legacy_aggregate_identity_migrates_dormant_references_before_restore() {
+    const BASE: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\n";
+    const WITH_SAVED: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\ntable saved:\n  target: totals\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = engine(WITH_SAVED);
+    seed(&mut e, "entries", serde_json::json!({"id":"e","n":7}));
+    let digest = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap()[0].field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
+    seed(&mut e, "saved", serde_json::json!({"id":"s","target":digest}));
+
+    // Model a release-store row written by 0.4.28, before digest identities.
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let saved = e.schema().tables["saved"].clone();
+    let old_target = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let old_saved = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let mut legacy_target = old_target.clone();
+    let mut legacy_saved = old_saved.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_target { fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone())); }
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_saved { fields.insert("target".into(), Value::Id(legacy)); }
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("saved", &saved, &old_saved).unwrap();
+    tx.put("saved", &saved, &legacy_saved, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old_target).unwrap();
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &legacy_target, None).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    // Removing `saved` retains it outside the active namespace while the
+    // aggregate target remains active. Identity adoption must rewrite both
+    // the hidden row and its dormant-reference ledger before setting marker.
+    activate(&mut e, BASE, 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    activate(&mut e, WITH_SAVED, 3).unwrap();
+    let restored = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(restored.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(restored[0].field("target").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest));
+}
+
 #[test]
 fn rollback_replaces_newer_actions_on_a_reference_that_stays_active() {
     let base = "table parents:\n  n: int\n  read <- allow\n  delete <- allow\n  sync public\nmutation drop():\n  delete parents['p']\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete keep\n  cap 4 by parent\n  read <- allow\n  sync public\n";

+    fn final_exists_holds(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: &Value, constraint: &Constraint) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
+        let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { return Ok(true);
+        };
+        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated").clone();

+            let rule = crate::schema::RuleExpr::Exists { table: target.clone(), index: index.clone(), key: key.clone(), equalities: vec![], provenance: crate::ir::KeyProvenance::Shape };
+            for term in key { if let crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) = term { self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field); } }
+            let Some(key) = self.final_reference_key(table_name, &rule, row)? else { return Ok(false);
+            };

+    /// Seed imports historically do not enforce every final-exists clause.
+    /// Capture only clauses that currently hold so seeded expiry retirement
+    /// can prove that its own reference actions did not invalidate them.
+    pub(super) fn satisfied_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<FinalExistsWitness>, RuntimeError> {
+        let inserted = self.inserted.clone();
+        let mut witnesses = Vec::new();
+        for (table, row) in inserted {
+            let constraints = self.schema.table(&table).expect("validated").constraints.clone();
+            for (constraint, clause) in constraints.iter().enumerate() {
+                if matches!(clause, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. })
+                    && self.final_exists_holds(&table, &row, clause)? {
+                    witnesses.push(FinalExistsWitness { table: table.clone(), row: row.clone(), constraint });
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(witnesses)
+    }

+    pub(super) fn check_final_exists_witnesses(&mut self, witnesses: &[FinalExistsWitness]) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

+            let constraint = self.schema.table(&witness.table).expect("validated")
+                .constraints.get(witness.constraint).expect("captured constraint").clone();
+            if !self.final_exists_holds(&witness.table, &witness.row, &constraint)? {
+                return Err(Self::final_exists_refusal(&witness.table, &constraint));
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }

     8	fn lifetime_changed(schema: &Schema, previous: &Schema, parent: &str) -> bool {
     9	    let old = previous.table(parent);
    10	    let new = schema.table(parent);
    11	    old.and_then(|t| t.expire.as_ref()) != new.and_then(|t| t.expire.as_ref())
    12	        || old.and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref()) != new.and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref())
    13	        || old.into_iter().chain(new).filter_map(|t| t.expire.as_ref()).any(|field|
    14	            crate::successor::interpretation(previous, parent, field) != crate::successor::interpretation(schema, parent, field))
    15	}

    17	pub(super) fn changed_parents(schema: &Schema, previous: Option<&Schema>) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    18	    let mut parents = BTreeSet::new();
    19	    for m in schema.maintains.iter().chain(previous.into_iter().flat_map(|s| &s.maintains)) {
    20	        let Some(owner) = &m.private else { continue };
    21	        if previous.is_none_or(|old| old.table(&owner.table).map(|t| &t.maintained) != schema.table(&owner.table).map(|t| &t.maintained)
    22	            || lifetime_changed(schema, old, &owner.table)
    23	            || schema.maintain_for(&m.target).is_some_and(|next| crate::successor::maintain_rebuild_needed(old, schema, next))) {
    24	            parents.insert(owner.table.clone());
    25	        }
    26	    }
    27	    parents
    28	}

    63	        let owner = m.private.as_ref().expect("private maintain");
    64	        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();

    75	                self.mirror_column(m, &group, total)?;
    76	            }
    77	        }
    78	        Ok(())

    70	    let name = format!("sb4_eval_maintained_id_{:x}", crate::ids::seed());
    71	    let mut engine = PostgresEngine::create(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name, schema, programs).unwrap();
    72	    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
    73	    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
    74	    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
    75	    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
    76	    let generation = engine.generation();
    77	    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
    78	    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
    79	    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
    80	    let mut old = old;
    81	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
    82	        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
    83	    }
    84	    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
    85	    let pointer_table = engine.schema.tables["pointers"].clone();
    86	    tx.put("pointers", &pointer_table, &object([("id", Value::Id("pointer".into())), ("total", Value::Id(legacy.clone()))]), None).unwrap();
    87	    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
    88	    tx.commit().unwrap();
    89	    drop(engine);

    91	    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();

NOT READY

- **PostgreSQL adoption leaves private aggregate totals under legacy ids.** [maintained_identity_upgrade.rs:20](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs:20) excludes private maintains, although [postgres/mod.rs:487](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/mod.rs:487) admits maintained columns over non-expiring read-through sources. Reopening publishes the current marker without rebuilding those totals. Subsequent maintenance looks up the digest address and starts from zero: adding a third contribution to a legacy count of two produces one; deleting a contribution can produce −1. Private-only schemas also miss the identity-related generation advance. Rebuild their private totals and mirrors before publishing the marker.

- **Commit-end prediction bypasses the device allowance for nested coverage work.** [local.rs:134](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/local.rs:134) enters `device_work`, taking `device_allowance`. Inside retirement, [write_references.rs:46](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write_references.rs:46) replaces that bounded meter with an unbounded meter. The coverage proof at [write_references.rs:202](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write_references.rs:202) then invokes nested `device_work`, whose missing-allowance branch executes directly ([local.rs:247](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/local.rs:247)). Membership and lifetime-witness reads therefore run unbounded, and their charges disappear when the prepaid action scope restores its meter. These additional proof reads are outside the schema-fixed closure reservation, so prediction can succeed where allowance exhaustion must instead roll back with `E_PREDICT`.
